ओङ्कारपूर्वाः श्रुतयो मखे ऽस्मिन् तिष्ठन्ति रूपेण तपोधनानाम् ।
यज्ञो ऽश्वमेधः प्रवरः क्रतूनां मुख्यस्तथा सत्रिषु दैत्यनाथः ॥
65.m: “Preceded by the syllable Om, the Vedas abide in this sacrifice in the form of ascetics; / the sacrifice is the horse-sacrifice, the best among rites, and chief among the sacrificers is the lord of Daityas.”

65.s:
itthaṃ vacanamākarṇya dānavādhipatirvaśī /
sārghapātraḥ samabhyāgādyatra devaḥ sthito 'bhavat //
65.d:
इत्थं वचनमाकर्ण्य दानवाधिपतिर्वशी ।
सार्घपात्रः समभ्यागाद्यत्र देवः स्थितो ऽभवत् ॥
65.m: Hearing this speech, the self-controlled lord of the Dānavas, / taking a vessel of water for the arghya offering, approached the place where the god stood.

65.s:
tator'cya. devadeveśamarcyamarghādināsuraḥ /
bharadvājarṣiṇā sārdhaṃ yajñavāṭaṃ praveśayat //
65.d:
ततोर्ऽच्य। देवदेवेशमर्च्यमर्घादिनासुरः ।
भरद्वाजर्षिणा सार्धं यज्ञवाटं प्रवेशयत् ॥
65.m: Then, having worshipped the worshipful god of gods with water for hospitality and other offerings, the asura / led him into the sacrificial arena along with the sage Bharadvāja.

65.s:
praviṣṭamātraṃ deveśaṃ pratipūjya vadhānataḥ /
provāca bhagavan brūhi kiṃ dadmi tava mānada //
65.d:
प्रविष्टमात्रं देवेशं प्रतिपूज्य वधानतः ।
प्रोवाच भगवन् ब्रूहि किं दद्मि तव मानद ॥
65.m: As soon as the lord of the gods had entered, he worshipped him with attentive devotion / and said: “Speak, O Blessed One! What may I give to you, O granter of honor?”

65.s:
tato 'bravīt suraśreṣṭho daityarājānamavyayaḥ /
vihasya suciraṃ kālaṃ bharadvājamavekṣya ca //
65.d:
ततो ऽब्रवीत् सुरश्रेष्ठो दैत्यराजानमव्ययः ।
विहस्य सुचिरं कालं भरद्वाजमवेक्ष्य च ॥
65.m: Then the imperishable, foremost of the gods, smiling for a long time / and looking at Bharadvāja, said to the king of the Daityas:

65.s:
gurormadīyasya gurustasyāstyagniparigrahaḥ /
na sa dhārayate bhūmyāṃ pārakyāṃ jātavedasam //
65.d:
गुरोर्मदीयस्य गुरुस्तस्यास्त्यग्निपरिग्रहः ।
न स धारयते भूम्यां पारक्यां जातवेदसम् ॥
65.m: “My teacher’s teacher maintains the sacred fire; / he does not keep the sacred fire on ground that belongs to another.

65.s:
tadarthamabhiyāc'haṃ mama dānavapārthiva /
maccharīrapramāṇena dehi rājan padatrayam //
65.d:
तदर्थमभियाच्ऽहं मम दानवपार्थिव ।
मच्छरीरप्रमाणेन देहि राजन् पदत्रयम् ॥
65.m: For that purpose I make this request of mine, O king of the Dānavas: / grant me three paces measured by my body, O king!”

65.s:
surārervacanaṃ śrutvā balirbhāryāmavekṣya ca /
bāṇaṃ ca tanayaṃ vīkṣya idaṃ vacanamabravīt //
65.d:
सुरारेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा बलिर्भार्यामवेक्ष्य च ।
बाणं च तनयं वीक्ष्य इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
65.m: Hearing the words of the enemy of the gods, Bali looked at his wife / and looked at his son Bāṇa, and uttered these words:

65.s:
na kevalaṃ pramāṇena vāmano 'yaṃ laghuḥ priye /
yena kramatrayaṃ maurkhyād yācate buddhito 'pi ca //
65.d:
न केवलं प्रमाणेन वामनो ऽयं लघुः प्रिये ।
येन क्रमत्रयं मौर्ख्याद् याचते बुद्धितो ऽपि च ॥
65.m: “Not only in stature is this dwarf small, my dear; / he is small also in intellect, since out of foolishness he asks for only three paces!

65.s:
prayo vidhātālpadhiyāṃ narāṇāṃ bahiṣkṛtānāṃ ca mahānubhāgyaiḥ /
dhanādikaṃ bhūri na vai dadāti yatheha viṣṇorna bahuprayāsaḥ //
65.d:
प्रयो विधाताल्पधियां नराणां बहिष्कृतानां च महानुभाग्यैः ।
धनादिकं भूरि न वै ददाति यथेह विष्णोर्न बहुप्रयासः ॥
65.m: Generally the Creator does not grant abundant wealth and the like to men of small intellect / who are excluded from great fortune, just as here Viṣṇu makes no great effort.

65.s:
na dadāti vidhistasya yasya bhāgyaviparyayaḥ /
mayi dātari yaścāyamadya yācet padatrayam //
65.d:
न ददाति विधिस्तस्य यस्य भाग्यविपर्ययः ।
मयि दातरि यश्चायमद्य याचेत् पदत्रयम् ॥
65.m: Fate gives nothing to him whose fortune has turned; / for while I am the giver, he asks today for merely three paces!”

65.s:
ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ mahātmā bhūyo 'pyuvācātha hariṃ danūjaḥ /
yācasva viṣṇo gajavājibhūmiṃ dāsīhiraṇyaṃ yadabhīpsitaṃ ca //
65.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा भूयो ऽप्युवाचाथ हरिं दनूजः ।
याचस्व विष्णो गजवाजिभूमिं दासीहिरण्यं यदभीप्सितं च ॥
65.m: Having spoken these words, the noble descendant of Danu said again to Hari: / “Ask, O Viṣṇu, for elephants, horses, land, maidservants, gold, or whatever else is desired!

65.s:
bhavān yācayitā viṣṇo ahaṃ dātā jagatpatiḥ /
dāturyācayiturlajjā kathaṃ na syāt padatraye //
65.d:
भवान् याचयिता विष्णो अहं दाता जगत्पतिः ।
दातुर्याचयितुर्लज्जा कथं न स्यात् पदत्रये ॥
65.m: You are the requester, O Viṣṇu, and I, the lord of the world, am the giver; / how should there not be shame for both giver and requester over three paces?

65.s:
rasātalaṃ vā vṛthivīṃ bhuvaṃ nākamathāpi vā /
etabhyaḥ katamaṃ dadyāṃ sthānaṃ yācasva vāmana //
65.d:
रसातलं वा वृथिवीं भुवं नाकमथापि वा ।
एतभ्यः कतमं दद्यां स्थानं याचस्व वामन ॥
65.m: Rasātala, or the earth, the intermediate region, or heaven— / which of these realms shall I give? Ask, O Vāmana!”

65.s:
vāmana uvāca /
gajāśvabhūhiraṇyādi tadarthibhyaḥ pradīyatām /
etāvatā tvahaṃ cārthī dehi rājan padatrayam //
65.d:
वामन उवाच ।
गजाश्वभूहिरण्यादि तदर्थिभ्यः प्रदीयताम् ।
एतावता त्वहं चार्थी देहि राजन् पदत्रयम् ॥
65.m: Vāmana said: / “Let elephants, horses, land, gold, and the like be given to those who desire them. / I desire only this much: grant me three paces, O king.”

65.s:
ityevamukte vacane vāmanena mahāsuraḥ /
balirbhṛṅgāramādāya dadau viṣṇoḥ kramatrayam //
65.d:
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने वामनेन महासुरः ।
बलिर्भृङ्गारमादाय ददौ विष्णोः क्रमत्रयम् ॥
65.m: When these words had been spoken by Vāmana, the great asura / Bali, taking up a water jar, granted the three paces to Viṣṇu.

65.s:
pāṇau tu patite toye divyaṃ rūpaṃ cakāra ha /
trailokyakramaṇārthāya bahurūpaṃ jaganmayam //
65.d:
पाणौ तु पतिते तोये दिव्यं रूपं चकार ह ।
त्रैलोक्यक्रमणार्थाय बहुरूपं जगन्मयम् ॥
65.m: As soon as the water fell into his hand, he assumed a divine form, / multiform, composed of the universe, in order to stride across the three worlds.

65.s:
padbhyāṃ bhūmistathā jaṅghe nabhastrailokyavanditaḥ /
satyaṃ tapo jānuyugme ūrubhyāṃ merumandarau //
65.d:
पद्भ्यां भूमिस्तथा जङ्घे नभस्त्रैलोक्यवन्दितः ।
सत्यं तपो जानुयुग्मे ऊरुभ्यां मेरुमन्दरौ ॥
65.m: From his two feet came the earth, and likewise his shanks the sky, he who is praised by the three worlds; / truth and austerity were in his pair of knees, and Meru and Mandara in his thighs.

65.s:
viśvedevā kaṭībhāge maruto vastiśīrṣagāḥ /
liṅge sthito manmathaśca vṛṣaṇābhyāṃ prajāpatiḥ //
65.d:
विश्वेदेवा कटीभागे मरुतो वस्तिशीर्षगाः ।
लिङ्गे स्थितो मन्मथश्च वृषणाभ्यां प्रजापतिः ॥
65.m: The Viśvedevas were situated on his hips, the Maruts on the crown of his bladder; / Manmatha was located on his penis, and Prajāpati on his testicles.

65.s:
kukṣibhyāmarṇavāḥ sapta jaṭhare bhuvanāni ca /
valiṣu triṣu nadyaśca yajñāstu jaṭhare sthitāḥ //
65.d:
कुक्षिभ्यामर्णवाः सप्त जठरे भुवनानि च ।
वलिषु त्रिषु नद्यश्च यज्ञास्तु जठरे स्थिताः ॥
65.m: In his flanks were the seven oceans, and in his belly the worlds; / in the three folds of his skin were the rivers, and the sacrifices were stationed in his belly.

65.s:
iṣṭāpūrtādayaḥ sarvāḥ kriyāstatra tu saṃsthitāḥ /
pṛṣṭhasthā vasavo devāḥ skandhau rudrairadhiṣaṭhitau //
65.d:
इष्टापूर्तादयः सर्वाः क्रियास्तत्र तु संस्थिताः ।
पृष्ठस्था वसवो देवाः स्कन्धौ रुद्रैरधिषठितौ ॥
65.m: All rites such as iṣṭa and pūrta were situated there; / on his back were the divine Vasus, and his two shoulders were occupied by the Rudras.

65.s:
bāhavaśca diśaḥ sarvā vasavo 'ṣṭau kare smṛtāḥ /
hṛdaye saṃsthito brahmā kuliśo hṛdayāsthiṣu //
65.d:
बाहवश्च दिशः सर्वा वसवो ऽष्टौ करे स्मृताः ।
हृदये संस्थितो ब्रह्मा कुलिशो हृदयास्थिषु ॥
65.m: His arms were all the directions; the eight Vasus were held to be in his hands; / Brahmā was stationed in his heart, and the thunderbolt in the bones of his chest.

65.s:
śrīsamudrā uromadhye candramā manasi sthitaḥ /
grīvāditirdevamātā vidyāstadvalayasthitāḥ //
65.d:
श्रीसमुद्रा उरोमध्ये चन्द्रमा मनसि स्थितः ।
ग्रीवादितिर्देवमाता विद्यास्तद्वलयस्थिताः ॥
65.m: The ocean of Śrī was in the middle of his chest, and the moon was situated in his mind; / his neck was Aditi the mother of the gods, and the sciences were situated in its folds.

65.s:
mukhe tu sāgnayo viprāḥ saṃskārā daśanacchadāḥ /
dharmakāmārthamokṣīyāḥ śāstraḥ śaucasamanvitāḥ //
65.d:
मुखे तु साग्नयो विप्राः संस्कारा दशनच्छदाः ।
धर्मकामार्थमोक्षीयाः शास्त्रः शौचसमन्विताः ॥
65.m: In his mouth were the Brahmins with the sacred fires; the sacraments were his lips; / the treatises on duty, desire, wealth, and liberation were endowed with purity.

65.s:
lakṣmyā saha lalāṭasthāḥ śravaṇābhyāmathāśvinau /
śvāsastho mātariśvā ca marutaḥ sarvasaṃdhiṣu //
65.d:
लक्ष्म्या सह ललाटस्थाः श्रवणाभ्यामथाश्विनौ ।
श्वासस्थो मातरिश्वा च मरुतः सर्वसंधिषु ॥
65.m: Along with Lakṣmī, they were situated on his forehead; then the two Aśvins on his ears; / and Mātariśvan was stationed in his breath, and the Maruts in all his joints.

65.s:
sarvasūktāni daśānā jihvā devī sarasvatī /
candrādityau ca nayane pakṣmasthāḥ kṛttikādayaḥ //
65.d:
सर्वसूक्तानि दशाना जिह्वा देवी सरस्वती ।
चन्द्रादित्यौ च नयने पक्ष्मस्थाः कृत्तिकादयः ॥
65.m: All the hymns were his teeth; the goddess Sarasvatī was his tongue; / the moon and the sun were his eyes; the Kṛttikās and the others were situated on his eyelashes.

65.s:
śikhāyāṃ devadevasya dhruvo rājā nyaṣīdata /
tārakā romakūpebhyo romāṇi ca maharṣayaḥ //
65.d:
शिखायां देवदेवस्य ध्रुवो राजा न्यषीदत ।
तारका रोमकूपेभ्यो रोमाणि च महर्षयः ॥
65.m: King Dhruva sat upon the topknot of the god of gods; / the stars came from his hair follicles, and the great sages were his bodily hairs.

65.s:
guṇaiḥ sarvamayo bhūtvā bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ /
krameṇaikena jagatīṃ jahāra sacarācarām //
65.d:
गुणैः सर्वमयो भूत्वा भगवान् भूतभावनः ।
क्रमेणैकेन जगतीं जहार सचराचराम् ॥
65.m: Having become all-inclusive through his qualities, the Lord, the originator of beings, / took the world with its moving and unmoving beings in a single stride.

65.s:
bhūmiṃ vikramamāṇasya mahārūpasya tasya vai /
dakṣiṇo 'bhūt stanaścandraḥ sūryo 'bhūdatha cottaraḥ /
nakṣaścākramato nābhiṃ sūryendū savyadakṣiṇau //
65.d:
भूमिं विक्रममाणस्य महारूपस्य तस्य वै ।
दक्षिणो ऽभूत् स्तनश्चन्द्रः सूर्यो ऽभूदथ चोत्तरः ।
नक्षश्चाक्रमतो नाभिं सूर्येन्दू सव्यदक्षिणौ ॥
65.m: As he of magnificent form was striding across the earth, / his right breast became the moon, and then his left became the sun; / and as he stepped, the navel was [the center], with the sun and moon on the left and right.

65.s:
dvitīyena krameṇātha svarmaharjanatāpasāḥ /
krāntārdhārdhena vairājaṃ madhyenāpūryatāmbaram //
65.d:
द्वितीयेन क्रमेणाथ स्वर्महर्जनतापसाः ।
क्रान्तार्धार्धेन वैराजं मध्येनापूर्यताम्बरम् ॥
65.m: Then with a second step, Svar, Mahar, Jana, and Tapas / were traversed by half of it, and with its middle the cosmic space of Virāj was filled.

65.s:
tataḥ pratāpinā brahman bṛhadviṣṇvaṅghriṇāmbare /
brahmāṇḍodaramāhatya nirālokaṃ jagāma ha //
65.d:
ततः प्रतापिना ब्रह्मन् बृहद्विष्ण्वङ्घ्रिणाम्बरे ।
ब्रह्माण्डोदरमाहत्य निरालोकं जगाम ह ॥
65.m: Then, O Brahmin, by the glorious, vast foot of Viṣṇu in the sky, / striking the hollow of the cosmic egg, he went into the lightless void.

65.s:
viśvāṅghriṇā prasaratā kaṭāho bhedito balān /
kuṭilā viṣṇupāde tu sametya kuṭilā tataḥ //
65.d:
विश्वाङ्घ्रिणा प्रसरता कटाहो भेदितो बलान् ।
कुटिला विष्णुपादे तु समेत्य कुटिला ततः ॥
65.m: As the foot that encompasses all stretched forth, the shell [of the universe] was shattered by force; / then, meeting with the foot of Viṣṇu, the meandering river became curved.

65.s:
tasyā viṣṇupadītyevaṃ nāmākhyātamabhūnmune /
tathā suranadītyevaṃ tāmasevanta tāpasāḥ /
bhagavānapyasaṃpūrṇe tṛtīye tu krame vibhuḥ //
65.d:
तस्या विष्णुपदीत्येवं नामाख्यातमभून्मुने ।
तथा सुरनदीत्येवं तामसेवन्त तापसाः ।
भगवानप्यसंपूर्णे तृतीये तु क्रमे विभुः ॥
65.m: Hence her name was declared to be ‘Viṣṇupadī’, O sage, / and likewise as the ‘River of the Gods’ the ascetics revered her. / And though the third stride remained incomplete, the Lord, the all-pervading one,

65.s:
samabhyetya baliṃ prāha īṣat prasphuritādharaḥ /
ṛmād bhavati daityendra bandhanaṃ ghoradarśanam /
tvaṃ pūraya padaṃ tanme no ced bandhaṃ pratīccha bhoḥ //
65.d:
समभ्येत्य बलिं प्राह ईषत् प्रस्फुरिताधरः ।
ऋमाद् भवति दैत्येन्द्र बन्धनं घोरदर्शनम् ।
त्वं पूरय पदं तन्मे नो चेद् बन्धं प्रतीच्छ भोः ॥
65.m: approached Bali and said, with slightly quivering lower lip: / “From debt, O lord of Daityas, arises terrible bondage. / Do you fulfill that footstep of mine; if not, accept bondage, sir!”

65.s:
tanmurārivacaḥ śrutvā vihasyātha baleḥ sutaḥ /
bāṇaḥ prāhāmarapatiṃ vacanaṃ hetusaṃyutam //
65.d:
तन्मुरारिवचः श्रुत्वा विहस्याथ बलेः सुतः ।
बाणः प्राहामरपतिं वचनं हेतुसंयुतम् ॥
65.m: Hearing those words of the enemy of Mura, Bali's son, / Bāṇa, laughed and addressed the lord of the immortals with reasoned words.

65.s:
bāṇa uvāca /
kṛtvā mahīmalpatarāṃ jagatpate svāyaṃbhuvādibhuvanāni vai ṣaṭ /
kathaṃ baliṃ prārthayase suvistṛtāṃ yāṃ prāgbhavān no vipulāmathākarot //
65.d:
बाण उवाच ।
कृत्वा महीमल्पतरां जगत्पते स्वायंभुवादिभुवनानि वै षट् ।
कथं बलिं प्रार्थयसे सुविस्तृतां यां प्राग्भवान् नो विपुलामथाकरोत् ॥
65.m: Bāṇa said: / “Having made the earth very small, O Lord of the world, along with the six worlds beginning with Svāyambhuva, / how can you ask of Bali this immense [earth], which you did not make so vast beforehand?

65.s:
vibho sahī yāvatīyaṃ tvayādya sṛṣṭacā sametā bhuvanāntarālaiḥ /
dattā ca tātena hi tāvatīyaṃ kiṃ vākchalenaiṣa nibadhyate 'dya //
65.d:
विभो सही यावतीयं त्वयाद्य सृष्टचा समेता भुवनान्तरालैः ।
दत्ता च तातेन हि तावतीयं किं वाक्छलेनैष निबध्यते ऽद्य ॥
65.m: O all-pervading Lord, as much of this earth as was created today by you, together with the intermediate regions of the worlds, / just that much was indeed given by my father; why is he bound today by deceitful words?

65.s:
yā naiva śakya bhavatā hi pūrituṃ kathaṃ vitanyād ditijeśvaro 'sau /
śaktastu saṃpūjayituṃ murāre prasīda mā bandhanamādiśasva //
65.d:
या नैव शक्य भवता हि पूरितुं कथं वितन्याद् दितिजेश्वरो ऽसौ ।
शक्तस्तु संपूजयितुं मुरारे प्रसीद मा बन्धनमादिशस्व ॥
65.m: That which cannot be filled even by you, how could this lord of Diti's offspring provide? / Yet he is able to worship you, O enemy of Mura; be gracious, do not decree bondage!

65.s:
proktaṃ śrutau bhavatāpīśa vākyaṃ dānaṃ pātre bhavate saukhyadāyi /
deśe supuṇye varade yacca kāle taccāśeṣaṃ dṛśyate cakrapāṇe //
65.d:
प्रोक्तं श्रुतौ भवतापीश वाक्यं दानं पात्रे भवते सौख्यदायि ।
देशे सुपुण्ये वरदे यच्च काले तच्चाशेषं दृश्यते चक्रपाणे ॥
65.m: The utterance declared in the scripture was spoken also by you, O Lord: ‘A gift given to a worthy recipient brings happiness, / as also in a very auspicious place and at a boon-granting time’; all that is seen here, O discus-bearer.

65.s:
dānaṃ bhūmiḥ sarvakāmapradeyaṃ bhavān pātraṃ devadevo jitātmā /
kālo jyeṣṭhāmūlayoge mṛgāṅgaḥ kurukṣetraṃ puṇyadeśaṃ prasiddham //
65.d:
दानं भूमिः सर्वकामप्रदेयं भवान् पात्रं देवदेवो जितात्मा ।
कालो ज्येष्ठामूलयोगे मृगाङ्गः कुरुक्षेत्रं पुण्यदेशं प्रसिद्धम् ॥
65.m: The gift is the earth, which grants all desires; you are the recipient, the god of gods, master of the self; / the time is the moon in conjunction with Jyeṣṭhā and Mūla; the renowned holy place is Kurukṣetra.

65.s:
kiṃ vā devo 'smadvidhairbuddhihīnaiḥ śikṣāpanīyaḥ sādhu vāsādhu caiva /
svayaṃ śrutīnāmapi cādikarttā vyāpya sthitaḥ sadasad yo jagad vai //
65.d:
किं वा देवो ऽस्मद्विधैर्बुद्धिहीनैः शिक्षापनीयः साधु वासाधु चैव ।
स्वयं श्रुतीनामपि चादिकर्त्ता व्याप्य स्थितः सदसद् यो जगद् वै ॥
65.m: Or how can a god be instructed by people like us, devoid of intellect, regarding what is good or bad? / You yourself are the original author of even the scriptures, pervading the existing and non-existing world.

65.s:
kṛtvā pramāṇaṃ svayaseva hīnaṃ padatrayaṃ yācitavān bhuvaśca /
kiṃ tvaṃ na gṛhṇāsi jagattrayaṃ bho rūpeṇa lokatrayavanditena //
65.d:
कृत्वा प्रमाणं स्वयसेव हीनं पदत्रयं याचितवान् भुवश्च ।
किं त्वं न गृह्णासि जगत्त्रयं भो रूपेण लोकत्रयवन्दितेन ॥
65.m: Having made your own measure small, you asked for three paces of the earth; / why do you not take the three worlds, sir, with your form praised by the three worlds?

65.s:
nātrāścaryaṃ yajjagad vai samagraṃ kramatrayaṃ naiva pūrṇaṃ tavādya /
krameṇa tvaṃ laṅghayituṃ samartho līlāmetāṃ kṛtavān lokanātha //
65.d:
नात्राश्चर्यं यज्जगद् वै समग्रं क्रमत्रयं नैव पूर्णं तवाद्य ।
क्रमेण त्वं लङ्घयितुं समर्थो लीलामेतां कृतवान् लोकनाथ ॥
65.m: It is no wonder that the entire universe could not fill your three strides today; / you are capable of traversing it in a single stride, yet you have engaged in this sport, O Lord of the world.

65.s:
pramāṇahīnāṃ svayameva kṛtvā vasuṃdharāṃ mādhava padmanābha /
viṣṇo na badhnāsi baliṃ na dūre prabhuryadevecchati tatkaroti //
65.d:
प्रमाणहीनां स्वयमेव कृत्वा वसुंधरां माधव पद्मनाभ ।
विष्णो न बध्नासि बलिं न दूरे प्रभुर्यदेवेच्छति तत्करोति ॥
65.m: Having yourself made the earth without measure, O Mādhava, O lotus-navelled one, / O Viṣṇu, you do not bind Bali far away; whatever the Master wishes, that he does.”

65.s:
pulastya uvāca /
ityevamukte vacane bāṇena balisūnunā /
provāca bhagavān vākyamādikarttā janārdanaḥ //
65.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने बाणेन बलिसूनुना ।
प्रोवाच भगवान् वाक्यमादिकर्त्ता जनार्दनः ॥
65.m: Pulastya said: / When these words had been spoken by Bāṇa, the son of Bali, / the Lord Janārdana, the original creator, spoke these words.

65.s:
trivikrama uvāca /
yānyuktāni vacāṃsītthaṃ tvayā bāleya sāmpratam /
teṣāṃ vaica hetusaṃyuktaṃ śṛṇu pratyuttaraṃ mama //
65.d:
त्रिविक्रम उवाच ।
यान्युक्तानि वचांसीत्थं त्वया बालेय साम्प्रतम् ।
तेषां वैच हेतुसंयुक्तं शृणु प्रत्युत्तरं मम ॥
65.m: Trivikrama said: / “Those words that were thus spoken by you now, O son of Bali, / hear my reply to them, endowed with reason.

65.s:
pūrvamuktastava pitā mayā rājan padatrayam /
dehi mahyaṃ pramāṇena tadetat samanuṣṭhitam //
65.d:
पूर्वमुक्तस्तव पिता मया राजन् पदत्रयम् ।
देहि मह्यं प्रमाणेन तदेतत् समनुष्ठितम् ॥
65.m: Earlier your father was told by me, ‘O king, give me three paces / according to my measure’; and that very thing was undertaken.

65.s:
kiṃ na vetti pramāṇaṃ me balistava pitāsura /
prāyacchad yena niḥśaṅkaṃ mamānantaṃ kramatrayam //
65.d:
किं न वेत्ति प्रमाणं मे बलिस्तव पितासुर ।
प्रायच्छद् येन निःशङ्कं ममानन्तं क्रमत्रयम् ॥
65.m: Did your father, Bali the asura, not know my measure, / by which he fearlessly granted me three endless strides?

65.s:
satyaṃ krameṇa caikena krameyaṃ bhūrbhuvādikam /
balerapi hitārthāya kṛtametat kramatrayam //
65.d:
सत्यं क्रमेण चैकेन क्रमेयं भूर्भुवादिकम् ।
बलेरपि हितार्थाय कृतमेतत् क्रमत्रयम् ॥
65.m: It is true that in one stride I could traverse Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, and the rest; / yet this span of three strides was made for the benefit of Bali as well.

65.s:
tasmād yanmama bāleya tvatpitrāmbu kare mahat /
dattaṃ tenāyuretasya kalpaṃ yāvad bhaviṣyati //
65.d:
तस्माद् यन्मम बालेय त्वत्पित्राम्बु करे महत् ।
दत्तं तेनायुरेतस्य कल्पं यावद् भविष्यति ॥
65.m: Therefore, O son of Bali, because of that great water poured into my hand by your father, / his lifespan shall endure as long as a kalpa.

65.s:
gate manvantare bāṇa śrāddhadevasya sāmpratam /
sāvarṇike ca saṃprāpte balirindro bhaviṣyati //
65.d:
गते मन्वन्तरे बाण श्राद्धदेवस्य साम्प्रतम् ।
सावर्णिके च संप्राप्ते बलिरिन्द्रो भविष्यति ॥
65.m: When the present manvantara of Śrāddhadeva has passed, O Bāṇa, / and the Sāvarṇika [manvantara] has arrived, Bali will become Indra.”

65.s:
itthaṃ proktvā balisutaṃ bāṇaṃ devastrivikramaḥ /
provāca balimabhyetya vacanaṃ madhurākṣaram //
65.d:
इत्थं प्रोक्त्वा बलिसुतं बाणं देवस्त्रिविक्रमः ।
प्रोवाच बलिमभ्येत्य वचनं मधुराक्षरम् ॥
65.m: Having spoken thus to Bāṇa, the son of Bali, the god Trivikrama / approached Bali and spoke words of sweet syllables.

65.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca /
āpūraṇād dakṣiṇāyā gaccha rājan mahāphalam /
sutalaṃ nāma pātālaṃ vasa tatra nirāmayaḥ //
65.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
आपूरणाद् दक्षिणाया गच्छ राजन् महाफलम् ।
सुतलं नाम पातालं वस तत्र निरामयः ॥
65.m: The holy Lord said: / “Until the sacrificial fee is fulfilled, O king, go to the greatly fruitful / Pātāla named Sutala; live there free from affliction.

65.s:
baliruvāca /
sutale vasato nātha mama bhogāḥ kuto 'vyayāḥ /
bhaviṣyanti tu yenāhaṃ nivatsyāmi nirāmayaḥ //
65.d:
बलिरुवाच ।
सुतले वसतो नाथ मम भोगाः कुतो ऽव्ययाः ।
भविष्यन्ति तु येनाहं निवत्स्यामि निरामयः ॥
65.m: Bali said: / “As I dwell in Sutala, O Lord, whence will come my imperishable enjoyments / by virtue of which I may dwell free from affliction?”

65.s:
trivikrama uvāca /
sutalasthasya daityendra yāni bhogāni te 'dhunā /
bhivaṣyanti mahārhāṇi tāni vakṣyāmi sarvaśaḥ //
65.d:
त्रिविक्रम उवाच ।
सुतलस्थस्य दैत्येन्द्र यानि भोगानि ते ऽधुना ।
भिवष्यन्ति महार्हाणि तानि वक्ष्यामि सर्वशः ॥
65.m: Trivikrama said: / “For you who dwell in Sutala, O lord of Daityas, whatever enjoyments / of great worth there will be now, I shall tell them all to you.

65.s:
dānānyavidhittāni śrāddhānyaśrotriyāṇi ca /
tathādhītānyavratibhirdāsyanti bhavataḥ phalam //
65.d:
दानान्यविधित्तानि श्राद्धान्यश्रोत्रियाणि च ।
तथाधीतान्यव्रतिभिर्दास्यन्ति भवतः फलम् ॥
65.m: Gifts given without proper rites, ancestral offerings made without Vedic scholars, / and recitations studied by those without vows, will yield their fruit to you.

65.s:
tathānyamutsavaṃ puṇyaṃ vṛtte śakramahotsave /
dvārapratipadā nāma tava bhāvī mahotsavaḥ //
65.d:
तथान्यमुत्सवं पुण्यं वृत्ते शक्रमहोत्सवे ।
द्वारप्रतिपदा नाम तव भावी महोत्सवः ॥
65.m: Likewise, another holy festival after the Great Festival of Śakra has concluded, / a great festival named Dvārapratipadā, shall be yours.

65.s:
tatra tvāṃ naraśārdūlā hṛṣṭāḥ puṣṭāḥ svalaṅkṛtāḥ /
puṣpadīpapradānena arjayiṣyanti yatnataḥ //
65.d:
तत्र त्वां नरशार्दूला हृष्टाः पुष्टाः स्वलङ्कृताः ।
पुष्पदीपप्रदानेन अर्जयिष्यन्ति यत्नतः ॥
65.m: There, the best among men, joyful, well-nourished, and finely adorned, / will diligently worship you by offering flowers and lamps.”

65.s:
tatrotsavo sukhyatamo bhaviṣyati divāniśaṃ hṛṣṭajanābhirāmam /
yathaiva rājye bhavatastu sāmprataṃ tathaiva sā bhāvyatha kaumudī ca //
65.d:
तत्रोत्सवो सुख्यतमो भविष्यति दिवानिशं हृष्टजनाभिरामम् ।
यथैव राज्ये भवतस्तु साम्प्रतं तथैव सा भाव्यथ कौमुदी च ॥
65.m: There will be a most delightful festival, charming day and night with joyful people; / just as it is now in your realm, so too will that Kaumudī [festival] take place.

65.s:
ityevamuktvā madhuhā ditīśvaraṃ visarjayitvā sutalaṃ sabhāryam /
yajñaṃ samādāya jagāma tūrṇaṃ sa śakrasadbhāmarasaṃghajuṣṭam //
65.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा मधुहा दितीश्वरं विसर्जयित्वा सुतलं सभार्यम् ।
यज्ञं समादाय जगाम तूर्णं स शक्रसद्भामरसंघजुष्टम् ॥
65.m: Having spoken thus, the slayer of Madhu dismissed the lord of the Ditis together with his wife to Sutala, / and taking the sacrifice, he went swiftly to Indra's abode, frequented by hosts of immortals.

65.s:
dattvā maghone ca vibhustriviṣṭapaṃ kṛtvā ca devān makhabhāgabhoktṝn /
antardadhe viśvapatirmaharṣe saṃpaśyatāmeva murādhipānām //
65.d:
दत्त्वा मघोने च विभुस्त्रिविष्टपं कृत्वा च देवान् मखभागभोक्तॄन् ।
अन्तर्दधे विश्वपतिर्महर्षे संपश्यतामेव मुराधिपानाम् ॥
65.m: Having given heaven to Maghavan and made the gods partakers of their shares of sacrifices, / the lord of the universe vanished, O great sage, even while the chiefs of the suras were watching.

65.s:
svargaṃ gate dhātari vāsudeve śālvo 'surāṇāṃ mahatā balena /
kṛtvā puraṃ saubhamiti prasiddhaṃ tadāntarikṣe vicacāra kāmāt //
65.d:
स्वर्गं गते धातरि वासुदेवे शाल्वो ऽसुराणां महता बलेन ।
कृत्वा पुरं सौभमिति प्रसिद्धं तदान्तरिक्षे विचचार कामात् ॥
65.m: When the creator Vāsudeva had gone to heaven, Śālva, with a great army of asuras, / having built the famous city called Saubha, wandered through the sky at will.

65.s:
mayastu kṛtvā tripuraṃ mahātmā suvarṇatāmrāyasamagryasaukhyam /
satārakākṣaḥ saha vaidyutena saṃtiṣṭhate bhṛtyakalatravān saḥ //
65.d:
मयस्तु कृत्वा त्रिपुरं महात्मा सुवर्णताम्रायसमग्र्यसौख्यम् ।
सतारकाक्षः सह वैद्युतेन संतिष्ठते भृत्यकलत्रवान् सः ॥
65.m: And the great-souled Maya, having built Tripura, yielding the highest comfort of gold, copper, and iron, / together with Tārakākṣa and Vaidyuta, dwelt there surrounded by servants and wives.

65.s:
baṇo 'pi devena hṛte triviṣṭape baddhe balau cāpi rasātalasthe /
kṛtvā suguptaṃ bhuvi śoṇitākhyaṃ puraṃ sa cāste saha dānavendraiḥ //
65.d:
बणो ऽपि देवेन हृते त्रिविष्टपे बद्धे बलौ चापि रसातलस्थे ।
कृत्वा सुगुप्तं भुवि शोणिताख्यं पुरं स चास्ते सह दानवेन्द्रैः ॥
65.m: And Bāṇa, when heaven was seized by the god and Bali bound and placed in Rasātala, / built a well-protected city on earth named Śoṇita and dwelt there with the lords of the Dānavas.

65.s:
evaṃ purā cakradhareṇa viṣṇunā baddho balirvāmanarūpadhāriṇā /
śakrapriyārtha surakāryasiddhaye hitāya viprarṣabhagodvijānām //
65.d:
एवं पुरा चक्रधरेण विष्णुना बद्धो बलिर्वामनरूपधारिणा ।
शक्रप्रियार्थ सुरकार्यसिद्धये हिताय विप्रर्षभगोद्विजानाम् ॥
65.m: Thus of old Bali was bound by Viṣṇu, bearer of the discus, assuming the form of Vāmana, / for Indra's pleasure, for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose, and for the welfare of the best of Brahmins, cows, and the twice-born.

65.s:
prādurbhavaste kathito maharṣe puṇyaḥ śucirvāmanasyāghahārī /
śrute yasmin saṃsmṛte kīrtite ca pāpaṃ yāti prakṣayaṃ puṇyameti //
65.d:
प्रादुर्भवस्ते कथितो महर्षे पुण्यः शुचिर्वामनस्याघहारी ।
श्रुते यस्मिन् संस्मृते कीर्तिते च पापं याति प्रक्षयं पुण्यमेति ॥
65.m: The holy, pure incarnation of Vāmana, which removes sin, has been told to you, O great sage; / when it is heard, remembered, and praised, sin is destroyed and merit increases.

65.s:
etat proktaṃ bhavataḥ puṇyakīrtteḥ prādurbhāvo balibandho 'vyayasya /
yaccāpyanyan śrotukāmo 'si vipra tatprocyatāṃ kathayiṣyāmyaśeṣam //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe pañcaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyaḥ
65.d:
एतत् प्रोक्तं भवतः पुण्यकीर्त्तेः प्रादुर्भावो बलिबन्धो ऽव्ययस्य ।
यच्चाप्यन्यन् श्रोतुकामो ऽसि विप्र तत्प्रोच्यतां कथयिष्याम्यशेषम् ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे पञ्चषष्टितमो ऽध्यः
65.m:
This incarnation and the binding of Bali by the imperishable one, whose fame is holy, have been told to you; / and whatever else you wish to hear, O Brahmin, let it be spoken, and I shall tell it entirely.

Thus ends the sixty-fifth chapter in the holy Vāmanapurāṇa.

66.s:
nārada uvāca /
śrutaṃ yathā bhagavatā balirbaddho mahātmanā /
kiṃ tvastayanyattu praṣṭavyaṃ tacchrutvā kathayādya me //
66.d:
नारद उवाच ।
श्रुतं यथा भगवता बलिर्बद्धो महात्मना ।
किं त्वस्तयन्यत्तु प्रष्टव्यं तच्छ्रुत्वा कथयाद्य मे ॥
66.m: Nārada said: / It has been heard how Bali was bound by the exalted, great-souled one; / but there is something else to be asked; having heard it, tell me today.

66.s:
bhagavān devarājāya dattvā viṣṇustriviṣṭapam /
antardhānaṃ gataḥ kvāsau sarvātmā tāta kathyatām //
66.d:
भगवान् देवराजाय दत्त्वा विष्णुस्त्रिविष्टपम् ।
अन्तर्धानं गतः क्वासौ सर्वात्मा तात कथ्यताम् ॥
66.m: Having given heaven to the king of the gods, / where did that Viṣṇu, the self of all, go after vanishing, O dear one? Tell me.

66.s:
sutalasthaśca daityendraḥ kimakārṣīt tathā vada /
kā ceṣṭā tasya viprarṣe tanme vyākhyātumarhasi //
66.d:
सुतलस्थश्च दैत्येन्द्रः किमकार्षीत् तथा वद ।
का चेष्टा तस्य विप्रर्षे तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
66.m: And what did the lord of Daityas do while staying in Sutala? Tell [me] that. / What were his actions, O Brahmin sage? You ought to explain that to me.

66.s:
pulastya uvāca /
antardhāya surāvāsaṃ vāmano 'bhūdavāmanaḥ /
jagāma brahmasadanamadhiruhyoragāśanam //
66.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
अन्तर्धाय सुरावासं वामनो ऽभूदवामनः ।
जगाम ब्रह्मसदनमधिरुह्योरगाशनम् ॥
66.m: Pulastya said: / Having vanished from the abode of the gods, Vāmana ceased to be a dwarf, / and having mounted the devourer of serpents, he went to the abode of Brahmā.

66.s:
vāsudevaṃ samāyāntaṃ jñātvā brahmāvyayātmakaḥ /
samutthāyāyatha sauhārdāt sasvaje kamalāsanaḥ //
66.d:
वासुदेवं समायान्तं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्माव्ययात्मकः ।
समुत्थायायथ सौहार्दात् सस्वजे कमलासनः ॥
66.m: Learning that Vāsudeva was arriving, Brahmā, whose nature is imperishable, / the lotus-seated one, stood up and then embraced [him] out of affection.

66.s:
pariṣvajyārcya vidhinā vedhāḥ pūjādinā harim /
papraccha kiṃ cireṇeha bhavatāgamanaṃ kṛtam /
66.6 athovāca jagatsvāmī mayā kāryaṃ mahatkṛtam /
surāṇāṃ kratubhāgārthaṃ svayaṃbho balibandhanam //
66.d:
परिष्वज्यार्च्य विधिना वेधाः पूजादिना हरिम् ।
पप्रच्छ किं चिरेणेह भवतागमनं कृतम् ।
66.6 अथोवाच जगत्स्वामी मया कार्यं महत्कृतम् ।
सुराणां क्रतुभागार्थं स्वयंभो बलिबन्धनम् ॥
66.m:
Embracing Hari and worshipping him according to the rules with offerings and ceremonies,
Vedhas asked, 'Why have you come here after a long time?'

Then the Lord of the universe spoke, 'A great deed has been done by me,
for the sake of the gods' share of the sacrifice, O Self-born one: the binding of Bali.'

66.s:
pitāmahastad vacanaṃ śrutvā muditamānasaḥ /
kathaṃ kathamiti prāha tvaṃ māṃ darśitumarhasi //
66.d:
पितामहस्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा मुदितमानसः ।
कथं कथमिति प्राह त्वं मां दर्शितुमर्हसि ॥
66.m: Hearing that word, the grandfather was joyful in mind; / he said: "How, how? You ought to show me!"

66.s:
ityevamukte vacane bhagavān garuḍadhvajaḥ /
darśayāmāsa tadrūpaṃ sarvadevamayaṃ laghu //
66.d:
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने भगवान् गरुडध्वजः ।
दर्शयामास तद्रूपं सर्वदेवमयं लघु ॥
66.m: When that word had been spoken, the exalted one who has Garuḍa on his banner / showed that form composed of all the gods, quickly.

66.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ yojanāyutavistṛtam /
tāvānevordhvāmānena tato 'jaḥ praṇato 'bhavat //
66.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा पुण्डरीकाक्षं योजनायुतविस्तृतम् ।
तावानेवोर्ध्वामानेन ततो ऽजः प्रणतो ऽभवत् ॥
66.m: Having seen that lotus-eyed one extending ten thousand yojanas, / and of the same measure in height, the unborn one bowed down before him.

66.s:
tataḥ praṇamya suciraṃ sādhu sādhvityudīrya ca /
bhaktitamro mahādevaṃ padmajaḥ stotramīrayat //
66.d:
ततः प्रणम्य सुचिरं साधु साध्वित्युदीर्य च ।
भक्तितम्रो महादेवं पद्मजः स्तोत्रमीरयत् ॥
66.m: Then, having bowed for a long time, saying, "Excellent, excellent!" / the lotus-born one, softened by devotion, uttered a hymn of praise to the great god.

66.s:
oṃ namaste devādhideva vāsudeva ekaśṛṅga bahurūpa vṛṣākape bhūtabhāvatana surāsuravṛṣa surāsuramathana pītavāsaḥ śrīnivāsa asuranirmitānta amitanirmita kapila mahākapila viṣvaksena nārāyaṇa (5) dhruvadhvaja satyadhvaja khaṅgadhvaja tāladhvaja vaikuṇṭhaṃ puruṣottama vareṇya viṣṇo aparājita jaya jayanta vijaya kṛtāvarta mahādeva anāde ananta ādyāntamadhyanidhana purañjaya dhanañjaya śuciśrava pṛśnigarbha (10) kamalagarbha kamalāyatākṣa śrīpate viṣṇumūla mūlādhivāsa dharmādhivāsa dharmavāsa dharmādhyakṣa prajādhyakṣa gadādhara śrīdhara śrutidhara vanamālādhara lakṣmīdhara dharaṇīdhara padbhanāma (15) viriñje ārṣṭiṣeṇa mahāsena senādhyakṣa puruṣṭuta bahukalpa mahākalpa kalpanāmukha aniruddha sarvaga sarvātman dvādaśātmaka sūryātmaka somātmaka kālātmaka vyomātmaka bhūtātmaka (20) rasātmaka paramātman sanātana muñjakeśa harikeśa guḍākeśa keśava nīla sūkṣma sthūla pīta rakta śveta śvetādhivāsa raktāmbarapriya prītikara prītivāsa haṃsa nīlavāsa sīradhvaja sarvalokādhivāsa (25) kuśeśaya adhokṣaja govinda janārdana madhusūdana vāmana namaste /
sahasraśīrṣo 'si sahasradṛgasi sahasrapādo 'si tvaṃ kamalo 'si mahāpuruṣo 'si sahasrabāhurasi sahasramūrtirasi tvaṃ devāḥ prāhuḥ sahasravadanaṃ (30) tenamasta /
oṃ namaste viśvadeveśa viśvabhūḥ viśvātmaka viśvarūpa viśvasaṃbhava tvatto viśvāmidamabhavad brāhmaṇāstvanmukhebhyo 'bhavan kṣatriyā doḥsaṃbhūtāḥ ūruyugmād viso 'bhavan śūdrāścaraṇakamalebhyaḥ (35) nābhyā bhavato 'ntarikṣamajāyata indrāgnīvaktrato netrād bhānurabhūnmanasaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ ahaṃ prasādajastava krodhāt tryambakaḥ prāṇājjāto bhavato mātariśvā śiraso dyaurajāyata śrotrād diśo bhūriyaṃ caraṇādabhūtśrotrodbhavādiśobhavataḥ svayaṃbhonakṣatrāstejodbhavāḥ (40) mūrttayaścāmūrtayaśca sarve tvattaḥ samudbhūtāḥ /
ato viśvātmako 'si oṃ nāste puṣpahāso 'si mahāhāso 'si paramo 'si oṃ kāro 'si vaṣaṭkāro 'si svarāhākāro 'si vauṣaṭkāro 'si svadhākāro 'si vedamayo 'si tīrthamayo 'si yajamānamayo 'si (45) yajñamayo 'si sarvadhātāsi yajñabhoktāsi śukradhātāsi bhūrda bhuvarda svarda svarṇada goda amṛtado 'sīti /
oṃ brahmādirasi brahmayo 'si yajño 'si vedakāmo 'si vedyo 'si yajñadhāro 'si mahāmīno 'si mahāseno 'si mahāśirā asi /
(50) nṛkesaryasi hotāsi homyo 'si havyo 'si hūyamāno 'si hayamedho 'si potāsi pāvayitāsi pūto 'si pūjyo 'si dātāsi hanyamāno 'si hriyamāṇo 'si harttāsīti oṃ /
nītirasi netāsi agryo 'si viśvadhāmāsi śubhāṇḍo 'si dhruvo 'si āraṇeyo 'si (55) dhyāno 'si dhyeyo 'si jñeyo 'si jñāno 'si jñāno 'si yaṣṭāsi dāno 'si bhūmāsi īkṣyo 'si brahmāsi hotāsi udgātāsi gatimatāṃ gatirasi jñānināṃ jñānamasi yogināṃ yogo 'si mokṣagāmināṃ mokṣo 'si śrīmatāṃ śrīrasi gṛhyo 'si pātāsi paramasi (60) somo 'si sūryo 'si dīkṣāsi dakṣiṇāsi naro 'si trinayano 'si mahānayano 'si ādityaprabhavo 'si surottamo 'si śucirasi śukro 'si nabhosi nabhasyo 'si iṣo 'si ūrjo 'si saho 'si sahasyo 'si tapo 'si tapasyo 'si madhurasi (65) mādhavo 'si kālo 'si saṃkramo 'si vikramo 'si parākramo 'si aśvagrīvo 'si mahāmedho 'si śaṅkaro 'si hariśvoro 'si śaṃbhurasi brahmeśo 'si sūryo 'si mitrāvaruṇo 'si prāgvaṃśakāyo 'si bhṛtādirasi mahābhūto 'si ūrdhvakarmāsi karttāsi (70) sarvapāpavimocano 'si trivikramo 'si oṃ namas te
66.d:
ओं नमस्ते देवाधिदेव वासुदेव एकशृङ्ग बहुरूप वृषाकपे भूतभावतन सुरासुरवृष सुरासुरमथन पीतवासः श्रीनिवास असुरनिर्मितान्त अमितनिर्मित कपिल महाकपिल विष्वक्सेन नारायण (5) ध्रुवध्वज सत्यध्वज खङ्गध्वज तालध्वज वैकुण्ठं पुरुषोत्तम वरेण्य विष्णो अपराजित जय जयन्त विजय कृतावर्त महादेव अनादे अनन्त आद्यान्तमध्यनिधन पुरञ्जय धनञ्जय शुचिश्रव पृश्निगर्भ (10) कमलगर्भ कमलायताक्ष श्रीपते विष्णुमूल मूलाधिवास धर्माधिवास धर्मवास धर्माध्यक्ष प्रजाध्यक्ष गदाधर श्रीधर श्रुतिधर वनमालाधर लक्ष्मीधर धरणीधर पद्भनाम (15) विरिञ्जे आर्ष्टिषेण महासेन सेनाध्यक्ष पुरुष्टुत बहुकल्प महाकल्प कल्पनामुख अनिरुद्ध सर्वग सर्वात्मन् द्वादशात्मक सूर्यात्मक सोमात्मक कालात्मक व्योमात्मक भूतात्मक (20) रसात्मक परमात्मन् सनातन मुञ्जकेश हरिकेश गुडाकेश केशव नील सूक्ष्म स्थूल पीत रक्त श्वेत श्वेताधिवास रक्ताम्बरप्रिय प्रीतिकर प्रीतिवास हंस नीलवास सीरध्वज सर्वलोकाधिवास (25) कुशेशय अधोक्षज गोविन्द जनार्दन मधुसूदन वामन नमस्ते ।
सहस्रशीर्षो ऽसि सहस्रदृगसि सहस्रपादो ऽसि त्वं कमलो ऽसि महापुरुषो ऽसि सहस्रबाहुरसि सहस्रमूर्तिरसि त्वं देवाः प्राहुः सहस्रवदनं (30) तेनमस्त ।
ओं नमस्ते विश्वदेवेश विश्वभूः विश्वात्मक विश्वरूप विश्वसंभव त्वत्तो विश्वामिदमभवद् ब्राह्मणास्त्वन्मुखेभ्यो ऽभवन् क्षत्रिया दोःसंभूताः ऊरुयुग्माद् विसो ऽभवन् शूद्राश्चरणकमलेभ्यः (35) नाभ्या भवतो ऽन्तरिक्षमजायत इन्द्राग्नीवक्त्रतो नेत्राद् भानुरभून्मनसः शशाङ्कः अहं प्रसादजस्तव क्रोधात् त्र्यम्बकः प्राणाज्जातो भवतो मातरिश्वा शिरसो द्यौरजायत श्रोत्राद् दिशो भूरियं चरणादभूत्श्रोत्रोद्भवादिशोभवतः स्वयंभोनक्षत्रास्तेजोद्भवाः (40) मूर्त्तयश्चामूर्तयश्च सर्वे त्वत्तः समुद्भूताः ।
अतो विश्वात्मको ऽसि ओं नास्ते पुष्पहासो ऽसि महाहासो ऽसि परमो ऽसि ओं कारो ऽसि वषट्कारो ऽसि स्वराहाकारो ऽसि वौषट्कारो ऽसि स्वधाकारो ऽसि वेदमयो ऽसि तीर्थमयो ऽसि यजमानमयो ऽसि (45) यज्ञमयो ऽसि सर्वधातासि यज्ञभोक्तासि शुक्रधातासि भूर्द भुवर्द स्वर्द स्वर्णद गोद अमृतदो ऽसीति ।
ओं ब्रह्मादिरसि ब्रह्मयो ऽसि यज्ञो ऽसि वेदकामो ऽसि वेद्यो ऽसि यज्ञधारो ऽसि महामीनो ऽसि महासेनो ऽसि महाशिरा असि ।
(50) नृकेसर्यसि होतासि होम्यो ऽसि हव्यो ऽसि हूयमानो ऽसि हयमेधो ऽसि पोतासि पावयितासि पूतो ऽसि पूज्यो ऽसि दातासि हन्यमानो ऽसि ह्रियमाणो ऽसि हर्त्तासीति ओं ।
नीतिरसि नेतासि अग्र्यो ऽसि विश्वधामासि शुभाण्डो ऽसि ध्रुवो ऽसि आरणेयो ऽसि (55) ध्यानो ऽसि ध्येयो ऽसि ज्ञेयो ऽसि ज्ञानो ऽसि ज्ञानो ऽसि यष्टासि दानो ऽसि भूमासि ईक्ष्यो ऽसि ब्रह्मासि होतासि उद्गातासि गतिमतां गतिरसि ज्ञानिनां ज्ञानमसि योगिनां योगो ऽसि मोक्षगामिनां मोक्षो ऽसि श्रीमतां श्रीरसि गृह्यो ऽसि पातासि परमसि (60) सोमो ऽसि सूर्यो ऽसि दीक्षासि दक्षिणासि नरो ऽसि त्रिनयनो ऽसि महानयनो ऽसि आदित्यप्रभवो ऽसि सुरोत्तमो ऽसि शुचिरसि शुक्रो ऽसि नभोसि नभस्यो ऽसि इषो ऽसि ऊर्जो ऽसि सहो ऽसि सहस्यो ऽसि तपो ऽसि तपस्यो ऽसि मधुरसि (65) माधवो ऽसि कालो ऽसि संक्रमो ऽसि विक्रमो ऽसि पराक्रमो ऽसि अश्वग्रीवो ऽसि महामेधो ऽसि शङ्करो ऽसि हरिश्वोरो ऽसि शंभुरसि ब्रह्मेशो ऽसि सूर्यो ऽसि मित्रावरुणो ऽसि प्राग्वंशकायो ऽसि भृतादिरसि महाभूतो ऽसि ऊर्ध्वकर्मासि कर्त्तासि (70) सर्वपापविमोचनो ऽसि त्रिविक्रमो ऽसि ओं नमस् ते
66.m: Om! Homage to you, God of gods, Vāsudeva, Single-horned, Multiform, Vṛṣākapi, Origin of beings, Bull of gods and asuras, Destroyer of gods and asuras, Yellow-robed, Abode of Śrī, Destroyer of the creations of asuras, Creator of the immeasurable, Kapila, Mahākapila, Viṣvaksena, Nārāyaṇa, having a firm banner, having truth for a banner, sword-bannered, palm-bannered, Vaikuṇṭha, Supreme Person, the Choice, Viṣṇu, Unconquered, Victory, Jayanta, Vijaya, Maker of the whirlpool, Mahādeva, Beginningless, Endless, End of the beginning, end, and middle, Conqueror of citadels, Conqueror of wealth, Purity-famed, Pṛśnigarbha, Lotus-wombed, Lotus-eyed, Lord of Śrī, Root of Viṣṇu, Dwelling in the root, Abode of righteousness, Dwelling of righteousness, Overseer of righteousness, Overseer of creatures, Club-bearer, Śrīdhara, Preserver of the Śruti, Vanamālā-bearer, Bearer of Lakṣmī, Earth-bearer, Padmanābha, Viriñci, Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, Mahāsena, General of the army, Praised by many, of many aeons, of the great aeon, Beginning of creation, Aniruddha, All-pervading, Self of all, Twelvefold, Consisting of the sun, Consisting of the moon, Consisting of time, Consisting of space, Consisting of the elements, Consisting of essence, Supreme Self, Eternal, Muñja-haired, Hari-haired, Guḍākeśa, Keśava, Blue, Subtle, Gross, Yellow, Red, White, White-robed, Fond of red garments, Causing affection, Abode of love, Haṃsa, Blue-robed, Plow-bannered, Abode of all worlds, Dweller in the lotus, Adhokṣaja, Govinda, Janārdana, Madhusūdana, Vāmana, homage to you! / You are thousand-headed, you are thousand-eyed, you are thousand-footed; you are the lotus, you are the Great Person; you are thousand-armed, you are of a thousand forms. The gods call [you] thousand-faced; therefore homage to you! / Om! Homage to you, Lord of the Viśvedevas, Source of the universe, Self of the universe, Universal form, Origin of the universe! From you this entire universe arose: the Brahmins arose from your mouths, the Kṣatriyas were produced from your arms, from your pair of thighs arose the Vaiśyas, the Śūdras from your lotus-feet. From your navel the atmosphere was born; Indra and Agni from your mouth; from your eye the sun arose, from your mind the moon; I arose from your grace, and Tryambaka from your wrath; from your breath was born Mātariśvan; from your head heaven was born; from your ear the quarters; this earth arose from your foot; the quarters arose from your ear; O self-born one, the lunar mansions arose from your radiance. Forms and the formless, all have arisen from you. / Therefore you are the Self of all. Om, homage! You are the blossom-smile, you are the great laughter, you are the supreme; you are the syllable Om, you are the Vaṣaṭ call, you are the Svarāhā call, you are the Vauṣaṭ call, you are the Svadhā call. You consist of the Vedas, you consist of the tīrthas, you consist of the sacrificer, you consist of the sacrifice. You are the supporter of all, you are the consumer of the sacrifice, you are the placer of the seed; you are the giver of earth, the giver of the atmosphere, the giver of heaven, the giver of gold, the giver of cattle, the giver of nectar. / Om, you are the origin of Brahmā, you are composed of Brahman, you are sacrifice, you are fond of the Vedas, you are the knowable, you are the bearer of sacrifice, you are the great fish, you are Mahāsena, you are the great-headed one. / You are the Man-lion, you are the hotṛ, you are the object of oblation, you are the sacrificial offering, you are the oblation being offered, you are the horse-sacrifice, you are the potṛ, you are the purifier, you are the purified, you are the adorable, you are the giver, you are the one being slain, you are the one being carried away, you are the remover: Om! / You are polity, you are the leader, you are the foremost, you are the universal abode, you are the auspicious egg, you are the immovable, you are born of the churning-sticks; you are meditation, you are the object of meditation, you are the knowable, you are knowledge, you are knowledge, you are the sacrificer, you are the gift, you are plenitude, you are the visible, you are Brahmā, you are the hotṛ, you are the udgātṛ; you are the goal of those who move, you are the knowledge of the wise, you are the yoga of the yogins, you are the liberation of those bound for liberation, you are the splendour of the splendid, you are the comprehensible, you are the protector, you are the supreme; you are Soma, you are Sūrya, you are consecration, you are the sacrificial gift, you are Nara, you are the three-eyed one, you are the great-eyed one, you are the source of the suns, you are the best among the gods, you are pure, you are Śukra, you are Nabhas, you are Nabhasya, you are Iṣa, you are Ūrja, you are Sahas, you are Sahasya, you are Tapas, you are Tapasya, you are Madhu, you are Mādhava, you are time, you are transition, you are stride, you are valour; you are the Horse-necked one, you are the great intelligence, you are Śaṅkara, you are Hariśvara, you are Śambhu, you are the lord of Brahmā, you are the sun, you are Mitra and Varuṇa, you are the body of the eastern sacrificial hall, you are the beginning of beings, you are the gross element, you are the one of exalted deeds, you are the creator, you are the liberator from all sin, you are Trivikrama! Om, homage to you!

66.s:
pulastya uvāca /
itthaṃ stutaḥ padmavena viṣṇustapasvibhiścādbhutakārmakārī /
provāca devaṃ prapitāmahaṃ tu varaṃ vṛṇīṣvāmalasattvavṛtte //
66.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
इत्थं स्तुतः पद्मवेन विष्णुस्तपस्विभिश्चाद्भुतकार्मकारी ।
प्रोवाच देवं प्रपितामहं तु वरं वृणीष्वामलसत्त्ववृत्ते ॥
66.m: Pulastya said: / Thus praised by the lotus-born [Brahmā] and by the ascetics, Viṣṇu, performer of wondrous deeds, / said to the god, the great-grandfather: 'Choose a boon, O you of pure nature and conduct!'

66.s:
tamabravīt prītiyutaḥ pitāmaho varaṃ mamehādya vibho prayaccha /
rūpeṇa puṇyena vibo hyanena saṃsthīyatāṃ madbhavane murāre //
66.d:
तमब्रवीत् प्रीतियुतः पितामहो वरं ममेहाद्य विभो प्रयच्छ ।
रूपेण पुण्येन विबो ह्यनेन संस्थीयतां मद्भवने मुरारे ॥
66.m: Filled with joy, the grandfather said to him: 'Grant me a boon here today, O Lord! / By this sacred form, O Lord, Murāri, abide indeed in my mansion!'

66.s:
itthaṃ vṛte devavareṇa prādāt prabhustathāstviti tamavyayātmā /
tasthau hi rūpeṇa hi vāmanena saṃpūjyamānaḥ sadane svayaṃbhoḥ //
66.d:
इत्थं वृते देववरेण प्रादात् प्रभुस्तथास्त्विति तमव्ययात्मा ।
तस्थौ हि रूपेण हि वामनेन संपूज्यमानः सदने स्वयंभोः ॥
66.m: When asked thus by the foremost of the gods, the imperishable Lord granted it, saying: 'So be it.' / And in the form of Vāmana he remained, worshipped in the abode of the Self-born one.

66.s:
nṛtyanti tatrāpsarasāṃ samūhya gāyanti gītāni surendragāyanāḥ /
vidyādharāstūryarāṃśca vādayan stuvanti devāsurasiddhasaṅghāḥ //
66.d:
नृत्यन्ति तत्राप्सरसां समूह्य गायन्ति गीतानि सुरेन्द्रगायनाः ।
विद्याधरास्तूर्यरांश्च वादयन् स्तुवन्ति देवासुरसिद्धसङ्घाः ॥
66.m: There hosts of apsarases danced; singers of the king of the gods sang songs; / Vidyādharas sounded their instruments; and crowds of gods, asuras, and Siddhas sang praises.

66.s:
tataḥ samārādhya vibhuṃ surādhipaḥ pitāmaho dhautamalaḥ sa śuddhaḥ /
svarge viriñciḥ sadanāt supuṣpāṇyānīya pūjāṃ pracakāra viṣṇoḥ //
66.d:
ततः समाराध्य विभुं सुराधिपः पितामहो धौतमलः स शुद्धः ।
स्वर्गे विरिञ्चिः सदनात् सुपुष्पाण्यानीय पूजां प्रचकार विष्णोः ॥
66.m: Then, having worshipped the Lord, the lord of the gods, the grandfather Viriñci, cleansed of impurity and pure, / brought splendid flowers from his abode in heaven and performed the worship of Viṣṇu.

66.s: svarge sahasraṃ sa tu yojanānāṃ viṣṇoḥ pramāṇena hi vāmano 'bhūt tatrāsya śakraḥ pracakāra pūjāṃ svayaṃbhuvastulyaguṇāṃ maharṣe //
66.d: स्वर्गे सहस्रं स तु योजनानां विष्णोः प्रमाणेन हि वामनो ऽभूत् तत्रास्य शक्रः प्रचकार पूजां स्वयंभुवस्तुल्यगुणां महर्षे ॥
66.m: Indeed, in heaven Vāmana measured a thousand yojanas according to Viṣṇu's measure; / there Śakra worshipped him with an excellence equal to that of the Self-born one, O great sage.

66.s:
etat tavoktaṃ bhagavāṃstrivikramaścakāra yad devahitaṃ mahātmā /
rasātalastho ditijaścakāra yattacchṛṇuṣvādya vadāmi vipra //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe ṣaṭṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
66.d:
एतत् तवोक्तं भगवांस्त्रिविक्रमश्चकार यद् देवहितं महात्मा ।
रसातलस्थो दितिजश्चकार यत्तच्छृणुष्वाद्य वदामि विप्र ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे षट्षष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
66.m:
This has been told to you: what the Lord Trivikrama, the great soul, accomplished for the welfare of the gods. / Now listen, O Brahmin, as I tell what the son of Diti, dwelling in Rasātala, did.

Thus ends the sixty-sixth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

67.s:
pulastya uvāca /
gatvā rasātalaṃ daityo mahārhamaṇicitritam /
śuddhasphaṭisopānaṃ kārayāmāsa vai puram //
67.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
गत्वा रसातलं दैत्यो महार्हमणिचित्रितम् ।
शुद्धस्फटिसोपानं कारयामास वै पुरम् ॥
67.m: Pulastya said: / Having gone to Rasātala, the Daitya caused a city to be built, / adorned with precious gems, having steps of pure crystal.

67.s:
tatra madhye suvistīrmaḥ prāsādo vajravedikaḥ /
muktājālāntaradvāro nirmito viśvakarmaṇā //
67.d:
तत्र मध्ये सुविस्तीर्मः प्रासादो वज्रवेदिकः ।
मुक्ताजालान्तरद्वारो निर्मितो विश्वकर्मणा ॥
67.m: In the middle of it, a vast palace was built by Viśvakarman, / with an altar of diamonds and doorways set with lattice-work of pearls.

67.s:
tatrāste vividhān bhogān bhuñjan divyān sa mānuṣān /
nāmnā vindhyāvalītyevaṃ bhāryāsya dayitābhavat /
67.3 yuvatīnāṃ sahasrasya pradhānā śīlamaṇḍitā /
tayā saha mahātejā reme vairocanirmune //
67.d:
तत्रास्ते विविधान् भोगान् भुञ्जन् दिव्यान् स मानुषान् ।
नाम्ना विन्ध्यावलीत्येवं भार्यास्य दयिताभवत् ।
67.3 युवतीनां सहस्रस्य प्रधाना शीलमण्डिता ।
तया सह महातेजा रेमे वैरोचनिर्मुने ॥
67.m:
There he dwelt, enjoying various divine and human pleasures;
his beloved wife was known by the name of Vindhyāvalī.

Foremost among a thousand maidens, adorned with good character,
with her the son of Virocana, of great splendor, took delight, O sage.

67.s:
bhogāsaktasya daityasya vasataḥ sutale tadā /
daityatejoharaḥ prāptaḥ capātāle vai sudarśanaḥ //
67.d:
भोगासक्तस्य दैत्यस्य वसतः सुतले तदा ।
दैत्यतेजोहरः प्राप्तः चपाताले वै सुदर्शनः ॥
67.m: While that Daitya, attached to pleasures, was dwelling in Sutala, / Sudarśana, who robs the Daityas of their splendor, arrived in Pātāla.

67.s:
cakre praviṣṭe pātālaṃ dānavānāṃ pure mahān /
babhai halahalāśabdaḥ kṣubhitārṇavasaṃnibhaḥ //
67.d:
चक्रे प्रविष्टे पातालं दानवानां पुरे महान् ।
बभै हलहलाशब्दः क्षुभितार्णवसंनिभः ॥
67.m: When the discus entered Pātāla, a great clamor arose / in the city of the Dānavas, like an agitated ocean.

67.s:
taṃ ca śrutvā mahāśabdaṃ baliḥ khaṅgaṃ samādade /
āḥ kimetaditītthañca papracchāsurapuṅgavaḥ //
67.d:
तं च श्रुत्वा महाशब्दं बलिः खङ्गं समाददे ।
आः किमेतदितीत्थञ्च पप्रच्छासुरपुङ्गवः ॥
67.m: Hearing that great roar, Bali seized his sword; / and 'Ah! What is this?' the foremost of the asuras asked.

67.s:
tato vindhyāvalī prāha sāntvayantī nijaṃ patim /
kośe khaṅgaṃ samāveśya dharmapatnī śucivratā //
67.d:
ततो विन्ध्यावली प्राह सान्त्वयन्ती निजं पतिम् ।
कोशे खङ्गं समावेश्य धर्मपत्नी शुचिव्रता ॥
67.m: Then Vindhyāvalī, his lawful wife of pure vows, spoke, / soothing her husband and sheathing his sword:

67.s:
etad bhagavataścakraṃ daityacakrakṣayaṅkaram /
saṃpūjanīyaṃ daityendra vāmanasya mahātmanaḥ /
ityevamuktvā cārvaṅgī sārghapātrā viniryayau //
67.d:
एतद् भगवतश्चक्रं दैत्यचक्रक्षयङ्करम् ।
संपूजनीयं दैत्येन्द्र वामनस्य महात्मनः ।
इत्येवमुक्त्वा चार्वङ्गी सार्घपात्रा विनिर्ययौ ॥
67.m: "This is the discus of the Lord, which brings destruction to the hosts of Daityas; / it should be worshipped, O lord of Daityas, [the discus] of the great-souled Vāmana." / Having spoken thus, the lovely-limbed woman went out bearing a vessel of water for the guest-offering.

67.s:
athābhyāgāt sahasrāraṃ viṣṇoścakraṃ sudarśanam /
tato 'surapatiḥ prahvaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo mune /
saṃpūjya vidhivaccakramidaṃ stotramudīrayat //
67.d:
अथाभ्यागात् सहस्रारं विष्णोश्चक्रं सुदर्शनम् ।
ततो ऽसुरपतिः प्रह्वः कृताञ्जलिपुटो मुने ।
संपूज्य विधिवच्चक्रमिदं स्तोत्रमुदीरयत् ॥
67.m: Then the thousand-spoked discus of Viṣṇu, Sudarśana, arrived. / Thereupon, O sage, the lord of the asuras bowed low with joined hands, / worshipped the discus according to rule, and uttered this hymn:

67.s:
baliruvāca /
namasyāmi hareścakraṃ daityacakravidāraṇam /
sahasrāṃśuṃ sahasrābhaṃ sahasrāraṃ sunirmalam //
67.d:
बलिरुवाच ।
नमस्यामि हरेश्चक्रं दैत्यचक्रविदारणम् ।
सहस्रांशुं सहस्राभं सहस्रारं सुनिर्मलम् ॥
67.m: Bali said: / "I bow to Hari's discus, the destroyer of the hosts of Daityas, / thousand-rayed, of thousandfold splendor, thousand-spoked, and spotless.

67.s:
namasyāmi hareścakraṃ yasya nābhyāṃ pitāmahaḥ /
tuṇḍe triśūladhṛk śarva ārāmūle mahādrayaḥ //
67.d:
नमस्यामि हरेश्चक्रं यस्य नाभ्यां पितामहः ।
तुण्डे त्रिशूलधृक् शर्व आरामूले महाद्रयः ॥
67.m: I bow to Hari's discus, in whose navel is the Grandfather, / on whose point is Śarva the trident-bearer, and at the base of whose spokes are the great mountains.

67.s:
areṣu saṃsthitā devāḥ sendrāḥ sārkāḥ sapāvakāḥ /
jave yasya sthito vāyurāpogniḥ pṛthivī nabhaḥ //
67.d:
अरेषु संस्थिता देवाः सेन्द्राः सार्काः सपावकाः ।
जवे यस्य स्थितो वायुरापोग्निः पृथिवी नभः ॥
67.m: On its spokes dwell the gods along with Indra, the sun, and fire; / in its swift speed dwell wind, water, fire, earth, and sky.

67.s:
āraprānteṣu jīmūtāḥ saudāminyṛkṣatārakāḥ /
bāhmato munayo yasya bālakhilyādayastathā //
67.d:
आरप्रान्तेषु जीमूताः सौदामिन्यृक्षतारकाः ।
बाह्मतो मुनयो यस्य बालखिल्यादयस्तथा ॥
67.m: At the ends of the spokes are the clouds, lightning, and constellations of stars; / on the outside are the sages, the Bālakhilyas and others.

67.s:
tamāyudhavaraṃ vande vāsudevasya bhaktitaḥ /
yanme pāpaṃ śarīrotthaṃ vāgjaṃ mānasameva ca //
67.d:
तमायुधवरं वन्दे वासुदेवस्य भक्तितः ।
यन्मे पापं शरीरोत्थं वाग्जं मानसमेव च ॥
67.m: With devotion I bow to that best weapon of Vāsudeva. / Whatever sin of mine has arisen from body, speech, or mind,

67.s:
tanme dahasva dīptāṃśo viṣṇoścakra sudarśana /
yanme kulodbhavaṃ pāpaṃ paitṛkaṃ mātṛkaṃ tathā //
67.d:
तन्मे दहस्व दीप्तांशो विष्णोश्चक्र सुदर्शन ।
यन्मे कुलोद्भवं पापं पैतृकं मातृकं तथा ॥
67.m: burn that away for me, O bright-rayed one, O Sudarśana, discus of Viṣṇu! / Whatever sin has arisen from my family, paternal or maternal,

67.s:
tanme harasva tarasā namaste acyutāyudha /
ādhayo mama naśyantu vyādhayo yāntu saṃkṣayam /
tvannāmakīrtanāc cakra duritaṃ yātu saṃkṣayam //
ityevamuktvā matimān samabhyarcyātha bhaktitaḥ //
67.d:
तन्मे हरस्व तरसा नमस्ते अच्युतायुध ।
आधयो मम नश्यन्तु व्याधयो यान्तु संक्षयम् ।
त्वन्नामकीर्तनाच् चक्र दुरितं यातु संक्षयम् ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा मतिमान् समभ्यर्च्याथ भक्तितः ॥
67.m:
take that swiftly away for me; reverence to you, weapon of Acyuta! / May my mental anguish vanish, may my diseases come to an end; / from reciting your name, O discus, may evil be destroyed!"

Having spoken thus, the wise one then worshipped it with devotion,

67.s: saṃsmaran puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāsanam //
67.d: संस्मरन् पुण्डरीकाक्षं सर्वपापप्रणासनम् ॥
67.m: remembering the lotus-eyed one who destroys all sins.

67.s:
pūjitaṃ balinā cakraṃ kṛtvā nistejaso 'surān /
niścakrāmātha pātālād viṣuve dakṣime mune //
67.d:
पूजितं बलिना चक्रं कृत्वा निस्तेजसो ऽसुरान् ।
निश्चक्रामाथ पातालाद् विषुवे दक्षिमे मुने ॥
67.m: Having been worshipped by Bali and having stripped the asuras of their splendor, / the discus departed from Pātāla at the southern equinox, O sage.

67.s:
sudarśane nirgate tu balirviklavatāṃ gataḥ /
paramāmāpadaṃ prāpya sasmāra svapitāmaham //
67.d:
सुदर्शने निर्गते तु बलिर्विक्लवतां गतः ।
परमामापदं प्राप्य सस्मार स्वपितामहम् ॥
67.m: When Sudarśana had gone, Bali was overcome with dejection; / having fallen into great distress, he remembered his grandfather.

67.s:
sa cāpi saṃsmṛtaḥ prāptaḥ sutalaṃ dānaveśvaraḥ /
dṛṣṭvā tasthau mahātejāḥ sārghapātro balistadā //
67.d:
स चापि संस्मृतः प्राप्तः सुतलं दानवेश्वरः ।
दृष्ट्वा तस्थौ महातेजाः सार्घपात्रो बलिस्तदा ॥
67.m: And remembered by him, the lord of the Dānavas arrived in Sutala. / Seeing him, Bali of great splendor then stood with a vessel of water for the guest-offering.

67.s:
tamarcya vidhinā brahman pituḥ pitaramīśvaram /
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā idaṃ vacanamabravīt /
67.22 saṃsmṛto 'si mayā tāta suviṣaṇṇena cetasā tanme hitaṃ ca pathyaṃ ca śreyogryaṃ vada tāta me /
67.23 kiṃ kāryaṃ tāta saṃsāre vasatā puruṣoṇa hi /
kṛtena yena vai nāsya bandhaḥ samupajāyate /
67.24 saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ narāṇāmalpacetasām /
taraṇe yo bhavet potastanme vyākhyātumarhasi //
pulastya uvāca /
etadvacanamākarṇya tatpautrād dānaveśvaraḥ /
vicintya prāha vacanaṃ saṃsāre yadvitaṃ param // 67.26 //
67.d:
तमर्च्य विधिना ब्रह्मन् पितुः पितरमीश्वरम् ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
67.22 संस्मृतो ऽसि मया तात सुविषण्णेन चेतसा तन्मे हितं च पथ्यं च श्रेयोग्र्यं वद तात मे ।
67.23 किं कार्यं तात संसारे वसता पुरुषोण हि ।
कृतेन येन वै नास्य बन्धः समुपजायते ।
67.24 संसारार्णवमग्नानां नराणामल्पचेतसाम् ।
तरणे यो भवेत् पोतस्तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
एतद्वचनमाकर्ण्य तत्पौत्राद् दानवेश्वरः ।
विचिन्त्य प्राह वचनं संसारे यद्वितं परम् ॥ 67.26 ॥
67.m:
Having worshipped his lordly grandfather according to rule, O Brahmin, / with palms joined reverently he spoke this word:

"You were remembered by me, dear father, with a deeply dejected heart; therefore, dear father, tell me what is beneficial, wholesome, and the highest good.

What, dear father, ought to be done by a man living in the cycle of existence, / by the doing of which, indeed, no bondage arises for him?

You ought to explain to me that which would be a boat / for the crossing over of small-minded men sunken in the ocean of worldly existence."

Pulastya said: / Having heard this speech from his grandson, the lord of the Dānavas / reflected and spoke words regarding that which is the supreme good in saṃsāra.

67.s:
prahlāda uvāca /
sādhu dānavaśārdūla yatte jātā matistviyam /
pravakṣyāmi hitaṃ te 'dya tathāneyeṣāṃ hitaṃ bale //
67.d:
प्रह्लाद उवाच ।
साधु दानवशार्दूल यत्ते जाता मतिस्त्वियम् ।
प्रवक्ष्यामि हितं ते ऽद्य तथानेयेषां हितं बले ॥
67.m: Prahlāda said: / "Well done, O tiger among Dānavas, that such a thought has arisen in you! / I shall declare today what is beneficial to you and beneficial to others, O Bali.

67.s:
bhavajaladhigatānāṃ dvāndvavātāhatānāṃ sutaduhitṛkalatratrāṇabhārārditānām /
viṣamaviṣayatoye majjatāmaplāvānāṃ bhavati śaraṇameko viṣṇupoto narāṇām //
67.d:
भवजलधिगतानां द्वान्द्ववाताहतानां सुतदुहितृकलत्रत्राणभारार्दितानाम् ।
विषमविषयतोये मज्जतामप्लावानां भवति शरणमेको विष्णुपोतो नराणाम् ॥
67.m: For men who have entered the ocean of worldly existence, buffeted by the winds of the pairs of opposites, oppressed by the burden of protecting sons, daughters, and wives, / sinking without a raft in the turbulent waters of the sense-objects, the boat of Viṣṇu alone is the refuge.

67.s:
ye saṃśritā harimanantamanādimadhyaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ suraguruṃ śubhadaṃ vareṇyam /
śuddhaṃ khagendragamanaṃ kamalālayeśaṃ te dharmarājakaraṇaṃ na viśanti dhīrāḥ /
67.29 svapuruṣamabhivīkṣya pāśahastaṃ vadati yamaḥ kila tasya karṇamūle /
parihara madhusūdanaprannān prabhurahamanyanṛṇāṃ na vaiṣṇavānām //
67.d:
ये संश्रिता हरिमनन्तमनादिमध्यं नारायणं सुरगुरुं शुभदं वरेण्यम् ।
शुद्धं खगेन्द्रगमनं कमलालयेशं ते धर्मराजकरणं न विशन्ति धीराः ।
67.29 स्वपुरुषमभिवीक्ष्य पाशहस्तं वदति यमः किल तस्य कर्णमूले ।
परिहर मधुसूदनप्रन्नान् प्रभुरहमन्यनृणां न वैष्णवानाम् ॥
67.m:
"Those wise men who have taken refuge in Hari—the infinite, who has neither beginning nor middle, / Nārāyaṇa, the preceptor of the gods, the giver of auspiciousness, the most excellent, / the pure one, who rides the king of birds, the lord of her whose abode is the lotus—do not enter the court of the King of Dharma.

Looking upon his own servant who holds a noose in his hand, Yama, they say, speaks into his ear: / 'Leave alone those who have surrendered to Madhusūdana; I am the master of other men, not of the Vaiṣṇavas.'

67.s:
tathānyaduktaṃ narasattamena ikṣvākuṇā bhaktiyutena nūnam /
ye viṣṇubhaktāḥ puruṣāḥ pṛthivyāṃ yamasya te nirviṣayā bhavanti //
67.d:
तथान्यदुक्तं नरसत्तमेन इक्ष्वाकुणा भक्तियुतेन नूनम् ।
ये विष्णुभक्ताः पुरुषाः पृथिव्यां यमस्य ते निर्विषया भवन्ति ॥
67.m: Likewise another [teaching] was spoken by Ikṣvāku, the best of men, full of devotion: / 'Those men on earth who are devoted to Viṣṇu are beyond the reach of Yama.'

67.s:
sā jihvā yā hariṃ stauti taccittaṃ yattadarpitam /
tāveva kevalaṃ śalāghyau yau tatpūjākarau karau //
67.d:
सा जिह्वा या हरिं स्तौति तच्चित्तं यत्तदर्पितम् ।
तावेव केवलं शलाघ्यौ यौ तत्पूजाकरौ करौ ॥
67.m: That is a tongue which praises Hari; that is a mind which is offered to him; / those hands alone are praiseworthy which perform worship of him.

67.s:
nūnaṃ na tau karau proktau vṛkṣaśākhāgrapallavau /
na yau pūjituṃ śaktau haripādāmbujadvayam //
67.d:
नूनं न तौ करौ प्रोक्तौ वृक्षशाखाग्रपल्लवौ ।
न यौ पूजितुं शक्तौ हरिपादाम्बुजद्वयम् ॥
67.m: Surely those are not called hands, but the sprout-tips of tree branches, / which are unable to worship the two lotus feet of Hari.

67.s:
nūnaṃ tatkaṇṭhaśālūkamathavā pratijihvakā /
rogovānyo na sā jihvā yā na vakti harerguṇān //
67.d:
नूनं तत्कण्ठशालूकमथवा प्रतिजिह्वका ।
रोगोवान्यो न सा जिह्वा या न वक्ति हरेर्गुणान् ॥
67.m: Surely that is a tumor of the throat, or an uvula, / or some other disease—it is not a tongue which does not speak the virtues of Hari.

67.s:
śocanīyaḥ sa bandhūnāṃ jīvannapi mṛto naraḥ /
yaḥ pādapaṅkajaṃ viṣṇorna pūjayati bhaktitaḥ //
67.d:
शोचनीयः स बन्धूनां जीवन्नपि मृतो नरः ।
यः पादपङ्कजं विष्णोर्न पूजयति भक्तितः ॥
67.m: He is to be pitied by his kinsmen, a man who is dead though alive, / who does not with devotion worship the lotus foot of Viṣṇu.

67.s:
ye narā vāsudevasya satataṃ pūjane ratāḥ /
mṛtā api na śocyāste satyaṃ satyaṃ mayoditam //
67.d:
ये नरा वासुदेवस्य सततं पूजने रताः ।
मृता अपि न शोच्यास्ते सत्यं सत्यं मयोदितम् ॥
67.m: Those men who are constantly devoted to the worship of Vāsudeva, / even when dead are not to be mourned; truth, truth has been spoken by me.

67.s:
śārīraṃ mānasaṃ vāgjaṃ mūrtāmūrtaṃ carācaram /
dṛśyaṃ spṛsyamadṛśyañca tatsarvaṃ keśavātmakam //
67.d:
शारीरं मानसं वाग्जं मूर्तामूर्तं चराचरम् ।
दृश्यं स्पृस्यमदृश्यञ्च तत्सर्वं केशवात्मकम् ॥
67.m: Bodily, mental, born of speech, formed and unformed, moving and unmoving, / visible, tangible, and invisible—all that has Keśava as its self.

67.s:
yenārcito hi bhagavān caturdhā vai trivikramaḥ /
tenārcitā na saṃdeho lokāḥ sāmaradānavāḥ //
67.d:
येनार्चितो हि भगवान् चतुर्धा वै त्रिविक्रमः ।
तेनार्चिता न संदेहो लोकाः सामरदानवाः ॥
67.m: By him by whom the Lord Trivikrama has been worshipped in fourfold manner, / by him, beyond doubt, the worlds together with the gods and Dānavas have been worshipped.

67.s:
yatā ratnāni jaladherasaṃkhyeyāni putraka /
tathā guṇā hi devasya tvasaṃkhyātāstu cakriṇaḥ //
67.d:
यता रत्नानि जलधेरसंख्येयानि पुत्रक ।
तथा गुणा हि देवस्य त्वसंख्यातास्तु चक्रिणः ॥
67.m: Just as jewels of the ocean are countless, O child, / even so the virtues of the god, the wielder of the discus, are indeed immeasurable.

67.s:
ye śaṅkhacakrābjakaraṃ saśārṅgiṇaṃ khagendraketuṃ varadaṃ śriyaḥ patim /
samāśrayante bhavabhītināśanaṃ saṃsāragarte na patanti te punaḥ //
67.d:
ये शङ्खचक्राब्जकरं सशार्ङ्गिणं खगेन्द्रकेतुं वरदं श्रियः पतिम् ।
समाश्रयन्ते भवभीतिनाशनं संसारगर्ते न पतन्ति ते पुनः ॥
67.m: Those who take refuge in the giver of boons, the husband of Śrī, whose banner is the lord of birds, who holds the conch, discus, and lotus in hand, along with the Śārṅga bow, the destroyer of fear of worldly existence—they do not fall into the pit of saṃsāra again.

67.s:
yeṣāṃ manasi govindo nivāsī satataṃ bale /
na te paribhavaṃ yānti na mṛtyorudvijanti ca //
67.d:
येषां मनसि गोविन्दो निवासी सततं बले ।
न ते परिभवं यान्ति न मृत्योरुद्विजन्ति च ॥
67.m: Those in whose mind Govinda dwells constantly, O Bali, / do not suffer defeat, nor do they tremble at death.

67.s:
devaṃ sārṅgadharaṃ viṣṇuṃ ye prapannāḥ parāyaṇam /
na teṣāṃ yamasālokyaṃ na ca te narakaukasaḥ //
67.d:
देवं सार्ङ्गधरं विष्णुं ये प्रपन्नाः परायणम् ।
न तेषां यमसालोक्यं न च ते नरकौकसः ॥
67.m: Those who have taken refuge in the supreme goal, god Viṣṇu the holder of the Śārṅga bow—they have no dwelling in Yama's realm, nor are they inhabitants of hell.

67.s:
na tāṃ gatiṃ prāpnuvanti śrutiśāstraviśāradāḥ /
viprā dānavaśārdūla viṣṇubhaktā vrajanti yām //
67.d:
न तां गतिं प्राप्नुवन्ति श्रुतिशास्त्रविशारदाः ।
विप्रा दानवशार्दूल विष्णुभक्ता व्रजन्ति याम् ॥
67.m: Brahmins skilled in the Vedic scriptures do not attain that destination, / O tiger among Dānavas, to which the devotees of Viṣṇu go.

67.s:
yā gatirdaityaśārdūla hatānāṃ tu mahāhave /
tato 'dikāṃ gatiṃ yānti viṣṇubhaktā narottamāḥ //
67.d:
या गतिर्दैत्यशार्दूल हतानां तु महाहवे ।
ततो ऽदिकां गतिं यान्ति विष्णुभक्ता नरोत्तमाः ॥
67.m: The destination of those slain in great battle, O tiger among Daityas— / higher than that is the destination to which the devotees of Viṣṇu, the best of men, go.

67.s:
yā gatirdharmaśīlānāṃ sāttvikānāṃ mahātmanām /
sā gatirgaditā daitya bhagavatsevināmapi //
67.d:
या गतिर्धर्मशीलानां सात्त्विकानां महात्मनाम् ।
सा गतिर्गदिता दैत्य भगवत्सेविनामपि ॥
67.m: Whatever destination is declared for those of virtuous conduct, the sattvic, the great-souled— / that same destination is declared, O Daitya, for those who serve the Lord.

67.s:
sarvāvāsaṃ vāsudevaṃ sūkṣmamavyaktavigraham /
praviśanti mahātmānaṃ tadbhaktā nānyacetasaḥ //
67.d:
सर्वावासं वासुदेवं सूक्ष्ममव्यक्तविग्रहम् ।
प्रविशन्ति महात्मानं तद्भक्ता नान्यचेतसः ॥
67.m: Vāsudeva, the dwelling-place of all, subtle, whose form is unmanifest, / that great soul his devotees enter, having no other thought in mind.

67.s:
ananyamanaso bhaktyā ye namasyanti keśavam /
śucayaste mahātmānastīrthabhūtā bhavanti te //
67.d:
अनन्यमनसो भक्त्या ये नमस्यन्ति केशवम् ।
शुचयस्ते महात्मानस्तीर्थभूता भवन्ति ते ॥
67.m: Those who, with minds directed to none other, bow with devotion to Keśava— / pure are they, great-souled; they become tīrthas themselves.

67.s:
gacchan tiṣṭhan svapan jāgrat pibannaścannabhīkṣṇaśaḥ /
dhyāyan nārāyaṇaṃ yastu na tato 'nyo 'sti puṇyabhāk /
vaikuṇṭhaṃ khaḍgaparaśuṃ bhavabandhasamucchidam //
67.d:
गच्छन् तिष्ठन् स्वपन् जाग्रत् पिबन्नश्चन्नभीक्ष्णशः ।
ध्यायन् नारायणं यस्तु न ततो ऽन्यो ऽस्ति पुण्यभाक् ।
वैकुण्ठं खड्गपरशुं भवबन्धसमुच्छिदम् ॥
67.m: Walking, standing, sleeping, waking, drinking, or eating constantly, / he who meditates on Nārāyaṇa—no one else possesses more merit than he— / [meditates on] Vaikuṇṭha, the sword and axe cutting the bonds of mundane existence.

67.s:
praṇipatya yathānyāyaṃ saṃsāre na punarbhavet /
kṣetreṣu vasate nityaṃ krīḍannāste 'mitadyutiḥ //
67.d:
प्रणिपत्य यथान्यायं संसारे न पुनर्भवेत् ।
क्षेत्रेषु वसते नित्यं क्रीडन्नास्ते ऽमितद्युतिः ॥
67.m: Having bowed down [to him] according to rule, one will not be born again in saṃsāra. / He dwells perpetually in holy fields, sporting, possessing boundless splendour.

67.s:
āsīnaḥ sarvadeheṣu karmabhirna sa badhyate /
yeṣāṃ viṣṇuḥ priyontyante viṣṇoḥ satataṃ priyāḥ //
67.d:
आसीनः सर्वदेहेषु कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ।
येषां विष्णुः प्रियोन्त्यन्ते विष्णोः सततं प्रियाः ॥
67.m: Though residing in all bodies, he is not bound by actions. / Those to whom Viṣṇu is dear in the end are ever dear to Viṣṇu.

67.s:
na te punaḥ sambhavanti tadbhaktāstatparāyaṇāḥ /
dhyāyed dāmodaraṃ yastu bhaktinamror'cayeta vā //
67.d:
न ते पुनः सम्भवन्ति तद्भक्तास्तत्परायणाः ।
ध्यायेद् दामोदरं यस्तु भक्तिनम्रोर्ऽचयेत वा ॥
67.m: Devoted to him, wholly dedicated to him, they are not born again. / He who meditates on Dāmodara, or bows down in devotion and worships [him],

67.s:
na sa saṃsārapaṅke 'smin majjate dānaveśvara /
kalyamutthāya ye bhaktyā smaranti madhusūdanam /
stuvantyapyabhiśṛṇvanti durgaṇyatitaranti te //
67.d:
न स संसारपङ्के ऽस्मिन् मज्जते दानवेश्वर ।
कल्यमुत्थाय ये भक्त्या स्मरन्ति मधुसूदनम् ।
स्तुवन्त्यप्यभिशृण्वन्ति दुर्गण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥
67.m: does not sink into this mire of saṃsāra, O lord of the Dānavas. / Those who, rising at dawn, remember Madhusūdana with devotion, / praise him, and listen [to his praises], cross over difficult perils.

67.s:
harivākyāmṛtaṃ pītvā vimalaiḥ śrotrabhājanaiḥ /
prahṛṣyati mano yeṣāṃ durgāṇyatitaranti te //
67.d:
हरिवाक्यामृतं पीत्वा विमलैः श्रोत्रभाजनैः ।
प्रहृष्यति मनो येषां दुर्गाण्यतितरन्ति ते ॥
67.m: Having drunk the nectar of Hari's words with spotless vessels of the ears, / those whose mind rejoices cross over difficult perils.

67.s:
yeṣāṃ cakragadāpāṇau bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī /
te yānti niyataṃ sthānaṃ yatra yogeśvaro hariḥ //
67.d:
येषां चक्रगदापाणौ भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी ।
ते यान्ति नियतं स्थानं यत्र योगेश्वरो हरिः ॥
67.m: Those whose devotion to the wielder of the discus and mace is unswerving / go inevitably to the abode where Hari, the lord of yoga, resides.

67.s:
viṣṇukarmaprasaktānāṃ bhaktānāṃ yā parā gatiḥ /
sā tu janmasahasreṇa na tapobhiravāpyate //
67.d:
विष्णुकर्मप्रसक्तानां भक्तानां या परा गतिः ।
सा तु जन्मसहस्रेण न तपोभिरवाप्यते ॥
67.m: The supreme state of devotees intent on Viṣṇu's service / cannot be obtained even in a thousand births by ascetic practices.

67.s:
kiṃ japyaistasya mantrairvā kiṃ tapobhiḥ kimāśramaiḥ /
yasya nāsti parā bhaktiḥ satataṃ madhusūdane //
67.d:
किं जप्यैस्तस्य मन्त्रैर्वा किं तपोभिः किमाश्रमैः ।
यस्य नास्ति परा भक्तिः सततं मधुसूदने ॥
67.m: What use are muttered prayers or mantras to him, what use are penances, what use the hermitage stages, / who has no supreme devotion continually directed to Madhusūdana?

67.s:
vṛthā yajñā vṛtā vedā vṛthā dānaṃ vṛthā śrutam /
vṛthā tapaśca kīrtiśca yo dveṣṭi madhusūdanam //
67.d:
वृथा यज्ञा वृता वेदा वृथा दानं वृथा श्रुतम् ।
वृथा तपश्च कीर्तिश्च यो द्वेष्टि मधुसूदनम् ॥
67.m: Vain are the sacrifices, vain the Vedas, vain the gift, vain the learning, / and vain are asceticism and fame for him who hates Madhusūdana.

67.s:
kiṃ tasya bahurbharmantrairbhaktiryasya janārdane /
namo nārāyaṇāyeti mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ //
67.d:
किं तस्य बहुर्भर्मन्त्रैर्भक्तिर्यस्य जनार्दने ।
नमो नारायणायेति मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः ॥
67.m: What need does he have of many mantras, whose devotion is fixed on Janārdana? / 'Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa'—this mantra accomplishes all aims.

67.s:
viṣṇureva gatiryoṣāṃ kutasteṣāṃ parājayaḥ /
yeṣāmindīvaraśyāmo hṛdayastho janārdanaḥ //
67.d:
विष्णुरेव गतिर्योषां कुतस्तेषां पराजयः ।
येषामिन्दीवरश्यामो हृदयस्थो जनार्दनः ॥
67.m: When Viṣṇu alone is their refuge, whence can defeat come to them, / whose heart Janārdana, dark like a blue lotus, occupies?

67.s:
sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalyaṃ vareṇyaṃ varadaṃ prabhum /
nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya sarvakarmāṇi kārayet //
67.d:
सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्यं वरेण्यं वरदं प्रभुम् ।
नारायणं नमस्कृत्य सर्वकर्माणि कारयेत् ॥
67.m: Having bowed down to the lord Nārāyaṇa, the auspiciousness of all auspicious things, / the most excellent, the granter of boons, one should perform all rituals.

67.s:
viṣṭayo vyatipātāśca ye 'nye durnītisambhavāḥ /
te nāma smaraṇādviṣṇornāsaṃ yānti mahāsura //
67.d:
विष्टयो व्यतिपाताश्च ये ऽन्ये दुर्नीतिसम्भवाः ।
ते नाम स्मरणाद्विष्णोर्नासं यान्ति महासुर ॥
67.m: Inauspicious astrological periods, malign planetary combinations, and whatever else arises from misconduct— / they come to destruction from the remembrance of Viṣṇu's name, O great asura.

67.s:
tīrthakoṭisahasrāṇi tīrthakoṭiśatāni ca /
nārāyaṇapraṇāmasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
67.d:
तीर्थकोटिसहस्राणि तीर्थकोटिशतानि च ।
नारायणप्रणामस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥
67.m: A thousand crores of tīrthas, and a hundred crores of tīrthas, / do not equal a sixteenth part of a salutation to Nārāyaṇa.

67.s:
pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca /
tāni sarvāṇyavāpnoti viṣṇornāmānukīrtanāt //
67.d:
पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च ।
तानि सर्वाण्यवाप्नोति विष्णोर्नामानुकीर्तनात् ॥
67.m: Whatever tīrthas and holy abodes there are on earth, / one attains them all by chanting Viṣṇu's name.

67.s:
prāpnuvanti na tāṃllokān vratino vā tapasvinaḥ /
prāpyante ye tu kṛṣṇasya namaskāraparairna raiḥ //
67.d:
प्राप्नुवन्ति न तांल्लोकान् व्रतिनो वा तपस्विनः ।
प्राप्यन्ते ये तु कृष्णस्य नमस्कारपरैर्न रैः ॥
67.m: Men observant of vows or ascetics do not attain those realms / that are attained by men wholly dedicated to bowing down to Kṛṣṇa.

67.s:
yo 'pyanyadevatābhakto mithyārcayati keśavam /
so/'pi gacchati sādhūnāṃ sthānaṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ mahat //
67.d:
यो ऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्तो मिथ्यार्चयति केशवम् ।
सो।ऽपि गच्छति साधूनां स्थानं पुण्यकृतां महत् ॥
67.m: Even a devotee of another deity who falsely worships Keśava / still goes to the great abode of the righteous, performers of meritorious deeds.

67.s:
sātatyena hṛṣīkeśaṃ pūjayitvā tu yatphalam /
sucīrṇatapasāṃ nṝṇāṃ tatā phalaṃ na kadācana //
67.d:
सातत्येन हृषीकेशं पूजयित्वा तु यत्फलम् ।
सुचीर्णतपसां नॄणां तता फलं न कदाचन ॥
67.m: The fruit that comes from continually worshiping Hṛṣīkeśa / is never matched by the fruit of men of well-performed asceticism.

67.s:
trisandhyaṃ padmānābhaṃ tu ye smaranti sumedhasaḥ /
te labhantyupavāsasya phalaṃ nāsatyatra saṃśayaḥ //
67.d:
त्रिसन्ध्यं पद्मानाभं तु ये स्मरन्ति सुमेधसः ।
ते लभन्त्युपवासस्य फलं नासत्यत्र संशयः ॥
67.m: The wise who remember Padmanābha at the three junctures of the day / attain the fruit of fasting; there is no doubt about this.

67.s:
satataṃ śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā harimarcaya /
tatprasādāt parāṃ siddhiṃ bale prāpsyasi śāśvatīm //
67.d:
सततं शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा हरिमर्चय ।
तत्प्रसादात् परां सिद्धिं बले प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतीम् ॥
67.m: Continually worship Hari with action ordained by sacred tradition; / by his grace, O Bali, you will attain supreme, eternal perfection.

67.s:
tanmanā bhava tadbhaktastadyājī taṃ namaskuru /
tamevāśritya deveśaṃ sukhaṃ prāpyasi putraka //
67.d:
तन्मना भव तद्भक्तस्तद्याजी तं नमस्कुरु ।
तमेवाश्रित्य देवेशं सुखं प्राप्यसि पुत्रक ॥
67.m: Fix your mind on him, be devoted to him, sacrifice to him, bow down to him; / having taken refuge in that lord of gods alone, you will attain bliss, my child.

67.s:
ādyaṃ hyanantamajaraṃ harimavyayaṃ ca ye vai smarantyaharaharnṛvarā bhuvisthāḥ /
sarvatragaṃ śubhadaṃ brahmamayaṃ purāṇam te yānti vaiṣṇavapadaṃ dhruvamakṣayañca //
67.d:
आद्यं ह्यनन्तमजरं हरिमव्ययं च ये वै स्मरन्त्यहरहर्नृवरा भुविस्थाः ।
सर्वत्रगं शुभदं ब्रह्ममयं पुराणम् ते यान्ति वैष्णवपदं ध्रुवमक्षयञ्च ॥
67.m: Those foremost among men dwelling on earth who day after day remember Hari—the primeval, infinite, ageless, imperishable, / all-pervading, bestower of good, composed of brahman, ancient—reach the steadfast and imperishable realm of Viṣṇu.

67.s:
ye mānavā vigatarāgaparāparajñā nārāyaṇaṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ smaranti /
te dhautapāṇḍurapuṭā iva rājahaṃsāḥ saṃsārasāgarajalasya taranti pāram //
67.d:
ये मानवा विगतरागपरापरज्ञा नारायणं सुरगुरुं सततं स्मरन्ति ।
ते धौतपाण्डुरपुटा इव राजहंसाः संसारसागरजलस्य तरन्ति पारम् ॥
67.m: Those men free from passion, knowing the higher and the lower, who constantly remember Nārāyaṇa, the guru of the gods, / cross to the other shore of the waters of the ocean of saṃsāra like royal swans with bright white wings.

67.s:
dhyāyanti ye satatamacyutamīśitāraṃ niṣkalmaṣaṃ pravarapadmadalāyatākṣam /
dhyānena tena hatakilbaṣavedanāste mātuḥ payodhararasaṃ na punaḥ pibanti //
67.d:
ध्यायन्ति ये सततमच्युतमीशितारं निष्कल्मषं प्रवरपद्मदलायताक्षम् ।
ध्यानेन तेन हतकिल्बषवेदनास्ते मातुः पयोधररसं न पुनः पिबन्ति ॥
67.m: Those who constantly meditate on Acyuta, the ruler, the taintless, having wide eyes like excellent lotus petals— / their agony of sins destroyed by that meditation, they do not drink a mother's milk again.

67.s:
ye kīrtayanti varadaṃ varapadmanābhaṃ śaṅkhābjacakravaracāpagadāsihastam /
padmālayāvadanapaṅkajaṣaṭpadākhyaṃ nūnaṃ prayānti sadanaṃ madhughātinaste //
67.d:
ये कीर्तयन्ति वरदं वरपद्मनाभं शङ्खाब्जचक्रवरचापगदासिहस्तम् ।
पद्मालयावदनपङ्कजषट्पदाख्यं नूनं प्रयान्ति सदनं मधुघातिनस्ते ॥
67.m: Those who extol the giver of boons, the supreme Padmanābha, who holds in his hands the conch, lotus, discus, excellent bow, mace, and sword, / who is praised as the bee to the lotus face of Lakṣmī, surely go to the abode of the slayer of Madhu.

67.s:
śṛṇvanti ye bhaktiparā manuṣyāḥ saṃkīrtyamānaṃ bhagavantamādyam /
te muktapāpāḥ sukhino bhavanti yathāmṛtaprāśanatarpitāstu //
67.d:
शृण्वन्ति ये भक्तिपरा मनुष्याः संकीर्त्यमानं भगवन्तमाद्यम् ।
ते मुक्तपापाः सुखिनो भवन्ति यथामृतप्राशनतर्पितास्तु ॥
67.m: Devoted human beings who listen to the praises of the primeval Lord / become freed from sin and happy, just like those satisfied by tasting nectar.

67.s:
tasmād dhyānaṃ smaraṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ vā nāmnāṃ śravaṇaṃ paṭhatāṃ sajjanānām /
kāryaṃ viṣṇoḥ śraddadhānairmanuṣyaiḥ pūjātulyaṃ tat praśaṃsanti devā //
67.d:
तस्माद् ध्यानं स्मरणं कीर्तनं वा नाम्नां श्रवणं पठतां सज्जनानाम् ।
कार्यं विष्णोः श्रद्दधानैर्मनुष्यैः पूजातुल्यं तत् प्रशंसन्ति देवा ॥
67.m: Therefore, meditation, remembrance, praise, or hearing the names [recited] by reciting good men / must be performed by faithful human beings for Viṣṇu; the gods extol that as equal to worship.

67.s:
bāhyaistathāntaḥkaraṇairaviklavairyo nārcayet keśavamīśitaram /
puṣpaiśca patrairjalapallavādibhirnūnaṃ sa muṣṭo vidhitaskareṇa //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe saptaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
67.d:
बाह्यैस्तथान्तःकरणैरविक्लवैर्यो नार्चयेत् केशवमीशितरम् ।
पुष्पैश्च पत्रैर्जलपल्लवादिभिर्नूनं स मुष्टो विधितस्करेण ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे सप्तषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
67.m:
He who does not worship Keśava, the ruler, with unagitated outer and inner faculties, / with flowers, leaves, water, and sprouts, has surely been robbed by the thief that is destiny.

Thus ends the sixty-seventh chapter in the glorious Vāmanapurāṇa.

68.s:
baliruvāca /
bhavatā kathitaṃ sarvaṃ samārādhya janārdanam /
yā gatiḥ prāpyate loke tāṃ me vaktumihārhasi //
68.d:
बलिरुवाच ।
भवता कथितं सर्वं समाराध्य जनार्दनम् ।
या गतिः प्राप्यते लोके तां मे वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
68.m: Bali said: / You have related everything about the state that is attained in the world by fully worshiping Janārdana; / you should now speak of it to me here.

68.s:
kenārcanena devasya prītiḥ samupajāyate /
kāni dānāni śastāni prīṇanāya jagadguroḥ //
68.d:
केनार्चनेन देवस्य प्रीतिः समुपजायते ।
कानि दानानि शस्तानि प्रीणनाय जगद्गुरोः ॥
68.m: By what manner of worship does the god's pleasure arise? / Which gifts are commended for pleasing the teacher of the universe?

68.s:
upavāsādikaṃ kāryaṃ kasyāṃ tithyāṃ mahodayam /
kāni puṇyāni śastāni viṣṇostuṣṭipradāni vai //
68.d:
उपवासादिकं कार्यं कस्यां तिथ्यां महोदयम् ।
कानि पुण्यानि शस्तानि विष्णोस्तुष्टिप्रदानि वै ॥
68.m: On what lunar day should fasting and the like be performed to yield great prosperity? / Which meritorious [deeds] are commended as giving satisfaction to Viṣṇu?

68.s:
yaccānyadapi karttavyaṃ hṛṣṭarūpairanālasaiḥ /
tadapyaśeṣaṃ daityendra mamākhyātumihārhasi //
68.d:
यच्चान्यदपि कर्त्तव्यं हृष्टरूपैरनालसैः ।
तदप्यशेषं दैत्येन्द्र ममाख्यातुमिहार्हसि ॥
68.m: And whatever else should be done by the joyful and diligent, / all that, too, O lord of Daityas, you should relate to me here.

68.s:
prahlāda uvāca /
śraddadhānairbhaktiparairyānyuddiśya janārdanam /
bale dānāni dīyante tānūcurmunayo 'kṣayān //
68.d:
प्रह्लाद उवाच ।
श्रद्दधानैर्भक्तिपरैर्यान्युद्दिश्य जनार्दनम् ।
बले दानानि दीयन्ते तानूचुर्मुनयो ऽक्षयान् ॥
68.m: Prahlāda said: / The gifts that are given for Janārdana, O Bali, by the faithful who are devoted, / sages have spoken of them as imperishable.

68.s:
tā eva tithayaḥ śastā yāsvabhyarcya jagatpatim /
taccittastanmayo bhūtvā upavāsī naro bhavet //
68.d:
ता एव तिथयः शस्ता यास्वभ्यर्च्य जगत्पतिम् ।
तच्चित्तस्तन्मयो भूत्वा उपवासी नरो भवेत् ॥
68.m: Those lunar days alone are commended on which a man, having worshiped the lord of the universe, / having set his mind on him and absorbed in him, fasts.

68.s:
pūjiteṣu dvijendreṣu pūjitaḥ syājjanārdanaḥ /
etān dviṣanti ye mūḍhāste yānti narakaṃ dhruvam //
68.d:
पूजितेषु द्विजेन्द्रेषु पूजितः स्याज्जनार्दनः ।
एतान् द्विषन्ति ये मूढास्ते यान्ति नरकं ध्रुवम् ॥
68.m: When the foremost twice-born are worshiped, Janārdana is worshiped; / those fools who hate them surely go to hell.

68.s:
tānarcayennaro bhaktyā brāhmaṇān viṣṇutatparaḥ /
evamāha hariḥ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇā māmakī tanuḥ //
68.d:
तानर्चयेन्नरो भक्त्या ब्राह्मणान् विष्णुतत्परः ।
एवमाह हरिः पूर्वं ब्राह्मणा मामकी तनुः ॥
68.m: A man dedicated to Viṣṇu should worship those Brahmins with devotion; / thus Hari declared long ago: 'The Brahmins are my own body.'

68.s:
brāhmaṇo nāvamantavyo budho vāpyabudho 'pi vā /
so 'pi divyā tanurviṣṇostasmāt tāmarcayennaraḥ //
68.d:
ब्राह्मणो नावमन्तव्यो बुधो वाप्यबुधो ऽपि वा ।
सो ऽपि दिव्या तनुर्विष्णोस्तस्मात् तामर्चयेन्नरः ॥
68.m: A Brahmin is not to be despised, whether learned or unlearned; / he too is the divine body of Viṣṇu; therefore a man should worship him.

68.s:
tānyeva ca praśastāni kusumāni mahāsura /
yāni syurvarṇayuktāni rasagandhayutāni ca //
viśeṣataḥ pravakṣyāmi puṣpāṇi tithayastathā /
dānāni ca praśastāni mādhavaprīṇanāya tu / /
68.d:
तान्येव च प्रशस्तानि कुसुमानि महासुर ।
यानि स्युर्वर्णयुक्तानि रसगन्धयुतानि च ॥
विशेषतः प्रवक्ष्यामि पुष्पाणि तिथयस्तथा ।
दानानि च प्रशस्तानि माधवप्रीणनाय तु । ।
68.m:
Those flowers alone are commended, O great asura, / which have [pleasing] colour and possess essence and fragrance.

In particular, I will proclaim the flowers, lunar days, / and praiseworthy gifts for the pleasing of Mādhava:

68.s:
68.11 jātī śatāhvā sumanāḥ kundaṃ bahupuṭaṃ tathā /
bāṇañca campakāśokaṃ karavīraṃ ca yūthikā //
68.d:
68.11 जाती शताह्वा सुमनाः कुन्दं बहुपुटं तथा ।
बाणञ्च चम्पकाशोकं करवीरं च यूथिका ॥
68.m: Jasmine, dill, Spanish jasmine, kunda, also the multi-layered [flower], / bāṇa, campaka, aśoka, oleander, and yūthikā.

68.s:
pāribhadraṃ pāṭalā ca bakulaṃ giriśālinī /
tilakaṃ ca japākusumaṃ pītakaṃ nāgaraṃ tvapi //
68.d:
पारिभद्रं पाटला च बकुलं गिरिशालिनी ।
तिलकं च जपाकुसुमं पीतकं नागरं त्वपि ॥
68.m: pāribhadra, pāṭalā, bakula, giriśālinī, / tilaka, japā-flower, pītaka, and nāgara.

68.s:
etāni hi praśastāni kusumānyacyutārcane /
surabhīṇi tathānyāni varjayitvā tu ketakīm //
68.d:
एतानि हि प्रशस्तानि कुसुमान्यच्युतार्चने ।
सुरभीणि तथान्यानि वर्जयित्वा तु केतकीम् ॥
68.m: For these flowers are recommended in the worship of Acyuta, / as are other fragrant ones, but excluding the ketakī.

68.s:
bilvapatraṃ śamīpatraṃ patraṃ bhṛṅgamṛgāṅkayoḥ /
tamālāmalakīpatraṃ śastaṃ keśavapūjane //
68.d:
बिल्वपत्रं शमीपत्रं पत्रं भृङ्गमृगाङ्कयोः ।
तमालामलकीपत्रं शस्तं केशवपूजने ॥
68.m: Bilva leaf, śamī leaf, the leaves of bhṛṅga and mṛgāṅka, / tamāla leaf, and āmalakī leaf are commended in the worship of Keśava.

68.s:
yeṣāmapi hica puṣpāṇi praśastānyacyutārcane /
pallavānyapi teṣāṃ stuḥ patrāṇyarcāvidhau hareḥ /
68.16 vīrudhāṃ ca pravālena barhiṣā cārcayettathā /
nānārūpaiścāmbubhavaiḥ kamalendīvarādibhiḥ //
68.d:
येषामपि हिच पुष्पाणि प्रशस्तान्यच्युतार्चने ।
पल्लवान्यपि तेषां स्तुः पत्राण्यर्चाविधौ हरेः ।
68.16 वीरुधां च प्रवालेन बर्हिषा चार्चयेत्तथा ।
नानारूपैश्चाम्बुभवैः कमलेन्दीवरादिभिः ॥
68.m:
Those whose flowers are praiseworthy in the worship of Acyuta, / their sprouts as well as leaves should also be used in the rite of worship of Hari.

And one should worship with shoots of creepers and with sacrificial grass, / and with water-born [blossoms] of diverse forms, such as the lotus, the blue water lily, and the rest.

68.s:
pravālaiḥ śucibhiḥ ślakṣṇairjalaprakṣālitairbale /
vanaspatīnāmarcyeta tathā dūrvāgrapallavaiḥ //
68.d:
प्रवालैः शुचिभिः श्लक्ष्णैर्जलप्रक्षालितैर्बले ।
वनस्पतीनामर्च्येत तथा दूर्वाग्रपल्लवैः ॥
68.m: O Bali, one should worship with pure, smooth shoots / of forest trees washed with water, and likewise with tips of dūrvā grass.

68.s:
candanenānulimpeta kuṅkumena prayatnanataḥ /
uśīrapadmakābhyāṃ ca tathā kālīyakādinā //
68.d:
चन्दनेनानुलिम्पेत कुङ्कुमेन प्रयत्ननतः ।
उशीरपद्मकाभ्यां च तथा कालीयकादिना ॥
68.m: One should diligently anoint [him] with sandalwood, with saffron, / with uśīra and padmaka, and likewise with kālīyaka and others.

68.s:
mahiṣākhyaṃ kaṇaṃ dāru sihlakaṃ sāgaruṃ sitā /
